parts.label: 1st metacarpal bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Metacarpal bones.g

card.name: 1st Metacarpal (Thumb)
card.summary: The metacarpal of the thumb. It is shorter and thicker than the others and is not tied to the second metacarpal, so the thumb moves freely.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the thumb (metacarpophalangeal joint)
landmarks: Two grooves on the palmar head for sesamoid bones
attachments: Abductor pollicis longus on the lateral side of the base
Opponens pollicis along the lateral shaft
First dorsal interosseous (part) on the shaft
Joint capsule and collateral ligaments of the metacarpophalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft, plus a growth plate at the base (it behaves like a phalanx). It fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: A break through the base that enters the joint (Bennett fracture) is unstable. Abductor pollicis longus pulls the shaft toward the wrist.
card.quiz: Shortest, thickest metacarpal; saddle joint with the trapezium.

parts.label: 2nd metacarpal bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Metacarpal bones.g

card.name: 2nd Metacarpal (Index)
card.summary: The metacarpal of the index finger. It is the longest metacarpal and forms the fixed, stable center of the hand.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the index finger (metacarpophalangeal joint)
attachments: Extensor carpi radialis longus on the back of the base
Flexor carpi radialis on the palmar base
Oblique head of adductor pollicis at the base
First and second dorsal interossei on the sides of the shaft
First palmar interosseous on the palmar shaft
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft; growth plate at the head. It fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Together with the third metacarpal it forms a rigid central pillar. Shaft fractures here are less common than at the 5th metacarpal.
card.quiz: Longest metacarpal; extensor carpi radialis longus inserts on its base.

parts.label: 3rd metacarpal bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Metacarpal bones.g

card.name: 3rd Metacarpal (Middle)
card.summary: The metacarpal of the middle finger. It sits in the center of the hand and has a small styloid process on its base.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the middle finger (metacarpophalangeal joint)
attachments: Extensor carpi radialis brevis on the styloid process of the base
Oblique head of adductor pollicis at the base
Transverse head of adductor pollicis along the palmar shaft
Second and third dorsal interossei on the sides of the shaft
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft; growth plate at the head. It fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Its styloid process can form a bony bump on the back of the wrist (carpal boss). The bump is often mistaken for a ganglion cyst.
card.quiz: Central metacarpal with a styloid process where extensor carpi radialis brevis attaches.

parts.label: 4th metacarpal bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Metacarpal bones.g

card.name: 4th Metacarpal (Ring)
card.summary: The metacarpal of the ring finger. Its base is more mobile than those of the 2nd and 3rd metacarpals.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the ring finger (metacarpophalangeal joint)
attachments: Third and fourth dorsal interossei on the sides of the shaft
Second palmar interosseous on the palmar shaft
No long forearm tendon inserts on this bone
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft; growth plate at the head. It fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: The neck of this bone can break after a punch, as can the 5th metacarpal. Rotation of the finger after a fracture must be checked.
card.quiz: Ring finger metacarpal; no forearm muscle tendon inserts on it.

parts.label: 5th metacarpal bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Metacarpal bones.g

card.name: 5th Metacarpal (Little)
card.summary: The metacarpal of the little finger. Its base is the most mobile, which lets the hand cup around an object.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the little finger (metacarpophalangeal joint)
attachments: Extensor carpi ulnaris on the tubercle of the base
Opponens digiti minimi along the ulnar shaft
Fourth dorsal interosseous and third palmar interosseous
Pisometacarpal ligament on the base
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft; growth plate at the head. It fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: A break through the neck, often after a punch, is called a boxer's fracture. The knuckle sinks and the finger can rotate.
card.quiz: Little finger metacarpal; extensor carpi ulnaris inserts on its base.

parts.label: Capitate bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Capitate
card.summary: The largest carpal bone, in the center of the wrist. Its rounded head fits into the cup formed by the scaphoid and lunate.
attachments: Oblique head of adductor pollicis (origin)
Palmar and dorsal intercarpal ligaments
Carpometacarpal ligaments
card.ossification: First carpal to ossify, at about 1 to 3 months of age.
card.clinical: Its head has a poor blood supply, like the scaphoid. It is the first carpal to ossify.
card.quiz: Largest carpal bone; the head sits in the scaphoid-lunate cup.

parts.label: Clavicle
parts.group: Skeletal system.g > Bones of upper limb.g > Bones of pectoral girdle.g

card.name: Clavicle (Collarbone)
card.summary: The S-shaped collarbone. It links the arm to the trunk and keeps the shoulder held out to the side.
articulations: Manubrium of sternum and first costal cartilage (sternoclavicular joint)
attachments: Sternocleidomastoid (clavicular head) on the upper medial third
Pectoralis major (clavicular head) on the front of the medial half
Deltoid on the front of the lateral third
Trapezius on the back of the lateral third
Subclavius in the groove on the underside
Coracoclavicular ligaments (conoid and trapezoid) on the underside of the lateral end
Costoclavicular ligament on the costal tuberosity
card.ossification: First bone in the body to begin ossifying (about week 5 of fetal life). The medial end fuses last, near age 25.
card.clinical: Fractures are common, usually at the junction of the middle and lateral thirds. The medial piece is often pulled upward by the sternocleidomastoid.
card.quiz: S-shaped bone that is the only bony link between the arm and the trunk.

parts.label: Distal phalanx of 1st finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Thumb - Distal Phalanx
card.summary: The last bone of the thumb. It supports the thumb pad and nail, and it has no middle phalanx before it.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the thumb (interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Flexor pollicis longus on the palmar base
Extensor pollicis longus on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Crush injuries can fracture the tuft. Cutting the flexor pollicis longus tendon prevents bending of the thumb tip.
card.quiz: Thumb tip bone; flexor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis longus insert here.

parts.label: Distal phalanx of 2nd finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Index Finger - Distal Phalanx
card.summary: The last bone of the index finger. It supports the fingertip pad and the nail.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the index finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Flexor digitorum profundus on the palmar base
Terminal tendon of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the distal interphalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Tearing the extensor tendon from its base causes mallet finger, and the tip cannot be straightened. Crush injuries can fracture the tuft.
card.quiz: Fingertip bone of the index finger; flexor digitorum profundus inserts on its palmar base.

parts.label: Distal phalanx of 3rd finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Middle Finger - Distal Phalanx
card.summary: The last bone of the middle finger. It supports the fingertip pad and the nail.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the middle finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Flexor digitorum profundus on the palmar base
Terminal tendon of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the distal interphalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Tearing the extensor tendon from its base causes mallet finger, and the tip cannot be straightened. Crush injuries can fracture the tuft.
card.quiz: Fingertip bone of the middle finger; flexor digitorum profundus inserts on its palmar base.

parts.label: Distal phalanx of 4th finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Ring Finger - Distal Phalanx
card.summary: The last bone of the ring finger. It supports the fingertip pad and the nail.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the ring finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Flexor digitorum profundus on the palmar base
Terminal tendon of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the distal interphalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: A forceful pull can tear flexor digitorum profundus from the base (jersey finger), and the tip cannot bend. The ring finger is most often involved.
card.quiz: Fingertip bone of the ring finger; flexor digitorum profundus inserts on its palmar base.

parts.label: Distal phalanx of 5th finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Little Finger - Distal Phalanx
card.summary: The last bone of the little finger. It supports the fingertip pad and the nail.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the little finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Flexor digitorum profundus on the palmar base
Terminal tendon of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the distal interphalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Tearing the extensor tendon from its base causes mallet finger, and the tip cannot be straightened. Crush injuries can fracture the tuft.
card.quiz: Fingertip bone of the little finger; flexor digitorum profundus inserts on its palmar base.

parts.label: Hamate bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Hamate
card.summary: A wedge-shaped carpal bone on the little-finger side of the distal row. It has a hook on its palmar surface.
attachments: Flexor retinaculum on the hook
Flexor digiti minimi brevis on the hook
Opponens digiti minimi on the hook
Pisohamate ligament
Pisometacarpal ligament
card.ossification: Begins ossifying at about 2 to 4 months of age.
card.clinical: The hook can fracture in golf, baseball and racquet sports. The ulnar nerve and flexor tendons next to it can be damaged.
card.quiz: Carpal with a palmar hook; articulates with the ring and little finger metacarpals.

parts.label: Humerus
parts.group: Skeletal system.g > Bones of upper limb.g > Bones of free part of upper limb.g

card.name: Humerus
card.summary: The long bone of the arm. It forms the shoulder joint above and the elbow joint below.
articulations: Scapula (glenohumeral joint, head into glenoid cavity)
Ulna (humeroulnar joint, trochlea into trochlear notch)
Radius (humeroradial joint, capitulum onto radial head)
attachments: Rotator cuff tendons on the tubercles (supraspinatus, infraspinatus, teres minor on greater; subscapularis on lesser)
Pectoralis major, latissimus dorsi and teres major along the intertubercular sulcus
Deltoid on the deltoid tuberosity
Coracobrachialis on the medial mid-shaft
Brachialis on the lower front of the shaft
Triceps (lateral and medial heads) on the back of the shaft
Common flexor origin on the medial epicondyle
Common extensor origin on the lateral epicondyle
Brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus on the lateral supracondylar ridge
card.ossification: Shaft ossifies before birth. Epiphyses appear in childhood, and the ends fuse to the shaft by about age 20.
card.clinical: A fracture of the surgical neck can injure the axillary nerve. A midshaft fracture can injure the radial nerve in the radial groove.
card.quiz: Long bone of the arm with a rounded head, a deltoid tuberosity and a spiral groove on the back.

parts.label: Lunate bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Lunate
card.summary: The crescent-shaped carpal bone in the middle of the proximal row. It sits in the lunate fossa of the radius at the wrist joint.
attachments: Scapholunate interosseous ligament
Lunotriquetral interosseous ligament
Palmar and dorsal radiocarpal ligaments
No muscles attach
card.ossification: Begins ossifying at about age 2 to 4 years.
card.clinical: It is the carpal bone most often dislocated, usually toward the palm. It can press on the median nerve and cause carpal tunnel symptoms.
card.quiz: Crescent-shaped carpal that most often dislocates toward the palm.

parts.label: Middle phalanx of 2nd finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Index Finger - Middle Phalanx
card.summary: The middle bone of the index finger. It lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the index finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
Distal phalanx of the index finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
landmarks: Ridges for the flexor digitorum superficialis
attachments: Flexor digitorum superficialis by two slips on the sides of the palmar shaft
Central slip of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joints
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Tearing the central slip at its base causes a boutonniere deformity. The proximal joint bends and the distal joint extends.
card.quiz: Middle bone of the index finger; flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on its shaft.

parts.label: Middle phalanx of 3rd finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Middle Finger - Middle Phalanx
card.summary: The middle bone of the middle finger. It lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the middle finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
Distal phalanx of the middle finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
landmarks: Ridges for the flexor digitorum superficialis
attachments: Flexor digitorum superficialis by two slips on the sides of the palmar shaft
Central slip of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joints
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: This bone and the one beside it are often hurt in ball sports. A torn central slip at the base gives a boutonniere deformity.
card.quiz: Middle bone of the middle finger; flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on its shaft.

parts.label: Middle phalanx of 4th finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Ring Finger - Middle Phalanx
card.summary: The middle bone of the ring finger. It lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the ring finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
Distal phalanx of the ring finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
landmarks: Ridges for the flexor digitorum superficialis
attachments: Flexor digitorum superficialis by two slips on the sides of the palmar shaft
Central slip of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joints
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Dislocation of the proximal interphalangeal joint is common in sport. Early movement helps prevent stiffness.
card.quiz: Middle bone of the ring finger; flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on its shaft.

parts.label: Middle phalanx of 5th finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Little Finger - Middle Phalanx
card.summary: The middle bone of the little finger. It lies between the proximal and distal phalanges.
articulations: Proximal phalanx of the little finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
Distal phalanx of the little finger (distal interphalangeal joint)
landmarks: Ridges for the flexor digitorum superficialis
attachments: Flexor digitorum superficialis by two slips on the sides of the palmar shaft
Central slip of the extensor expansion on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the interphalangeal joints
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: It is the shortest middle phalanx. The proximal interphalangeal joint is easily injured in sport.
card.quiz: Middle bone of the little finger; flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on its shaft.

parts.label: Pisiform bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Pisiform
card.summary: A small pea-shaped carpal bone on the little-finger side of the palm. It is a sesamoid bone inside the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.
landmarks: Single facet on the dorsal surface (for triquetrum)
Palmar prominence (palpable at the base of the hypothenar eminence)
attachments: Flexor carpi ulnaris tendon (insertion)
Abductor digiti minimi (origin)
Flexor retinaculum
Pisohamate ligament
Pisometacarpal ligament (to the base of the 5th metacarpal)
card.ossification: Last carpal to ossify, at about age 9 to 12 years.
card.clinical: The ulnar nerve and artery pass beside it through the ulnar tunnel (Guyon's canal). It can be fractured by a direct blow or fall.
card.quiz: Pea-shaped sesamoid carpal inside the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon.

parts.label: Proximal phalanx of 1st finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Thumb - Proximal Phalanx
card.summary: The first bone of the thumb beyond the metacarpal. The thumb has only two phalanges, a proximal and a distal.
articulations: Distal phalanx of the thumb (interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Abductor pollicis brevis on the lateral base
Flexor pollicis brevis on the lateral base
Adductor pollicis on the medial base (through a sesamoid bone)
Extensor pollicis brevis on the dorsal base
Collateral ligaments of the metacarpophalangeal joint
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Tearing the ulnar collateral ligament at its base (gamekeeper's or skier's thumb) makes pinching weak and painful.
card.quiz: Thumb phalanx between the first metacarpal and the distal phalanx.

parts.label: Proximal phalanx of 2nd finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Index Finger - Proximal Phalanx
card.summary: The first bone of the index finger beyond the metacarpal. It is the longest of the three phalanges of the finger.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the index finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: First dorsal interosseous on the radial side of the base
First palmar interosseous into the extensor expansion
Fibrous flexor sheath on the palmar shaft
Extensor expansion over the back
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: The proximal interphalangeal joint is often dislocated or sprained in ball sports. Trigger finger occurs when the tendon catches at the A1 pulley at the metacarpal head.
card.quiz: First phalanx of the index finger; it meets the metacarpal at the knuckle.

parts.label: Proximal phalanx of 3rd finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Middle Finger - Proximal Phalanx
card.summary: The first bone of the middle finger beyond the metacarpal. It is the longest of the three phalanges of the finger.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the middle finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Second and third dorsal interossei on the radial and ulnar sides of the base
Fibrous flexor sheath on the palmar shaft
Extensor expansion over the back
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Fractures of the proximal phalanx can heal with a rotated finger, which makes the fingers overlap when the fist is closed.
card.quiz: First phalanx of the middle finger; it meets the metacarpal at the knuckle.

parts.label: Proximal phalanx of 4th finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Ring Finger - Proximal Phalanx
card.summary: The first bone of the ring finger beyond the metacarpal. It is the longest of the three phalanges of the finger.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the ring finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Fourth dorsal interosseous on the ulnar side of the base
Second palmar interosseous into the extensor expansion
Fibrous flexor sheath on the palmar shaft
Extensor expansion over the back
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Shaft fractures often angle with the point toward the palm, because the interossei flex the upper fragment.
card.quiz: First phalanx of the ring finger; it meets the metacarpal at the knuckle.

parts.label: Proximal phalanx of 5th finger
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Phalanges of hand.g

card.name: Little Finger - Proximal Phalanx
card.summary: The first bone of the little finger beyond the metacarpal. It is the longest of the three phalanges of the finger.
articulations: Middle phalanx of the little finger (proximal interphalangeal joint)
attachments: Abductor digiti minimi on the ulnar side of the base
Flexor digiti minimi brevis on the base
Third palmar interosseous into the extensor expansion
Fibrous flexor sheath on the palmar shaft
Extensor expansion over the back
card.ossification: Primary center in the shaft before birth. The growth plate at the base fuses by about age 16 to 18.
card.clinical: Fractures are common in sport. After a break, check that the finger is not rotated, which makes it cross its neighbor.
card.quiz: First phalanx of the little finger; it meets the metacarpal at the knuckle.

parts.label: Radius
parts.group: Skeletal system.g > Bones of upper limb.g > Bones of free part of upper limb.g

card.name: Radius
card.summary: The lateral forearm bone, on the thumb side. It is small at the elbow and wide at the wrist, and it rotates around the ulna.
articulations: Ulna (proximal radioulnar joint, head in radial notch)
Ulna (distal radioulnar joint, ulnar notch around ulnar head)
Scaphoid and lunate (radiocarpal joint, the wrist joint)
attachments: Biceps brachii on the radial tuberosity
Supinator on the upper lateral shaft
Pronator teres on the pronator tuberosity (mid-lateral shaft)
Flexor digitorum superficialis on the anterior oblique line
Flexor pollicis longus on the front of the shaft
Pronator quadratus on the lower front of the shaft
Brachioradialis on the lower lateral end near the styloid process
Interosseous membrane on the interosseous border
Annular ligament around the head (attaches to the ulna)
card.ossification: Shaft ossifies before birth. The distal end appears at about age 1 and fuses by about age 20.
card.clinical: A fall on the outstretched hand can break the distal radius (Colles fracture), tilting the hand backward like a dinner fork. A child can pull the radial head out of the annular ligament (nursemaid's elbow).
card.quiz: Forearm bone on the thumb side with a disc-shaped head and a styloid process at the wrist.

parts.label: Scaphoid bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Scaphoid
card.summary: The boat-shaped carpal bone on the thumb side of the proximal row. It bridges the two rows of carpal bones.
attachments: Radial collateral ligament of the wrist
Flexor retinaculum on the tubercle
Scapholunate interosseous ligament
card.ossification: Begins ossifying at about age 4 to 6 years.
card.clinical: It is the most commonly fractured carpal bone, with pain in the anatomical snuffbox. Waist fractures can cut off the blood supply and cause bone death.
card.quiz: Boat-shaped carpal; tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after a fall.

parts.label: Scapula
parts.group: Skeletal system.g > Bones of upper limb.g > Bones of pectoral girdle.g

card.name: Scapula (Shoulder Blade)
card.summary: A flat, triangular bone on the back of the rib cage. It forms the socket of the shoulder joint and anchors many shoulder muscles.
articulations: Humerus (glenohumeral joint, at the glenoid cavity)
attachments: Rotator cuff: supraspinatus (supraspinous fossa), infraspinatus (infraspinous fossa), subscapularis (subscapular fossa), teres minor (lateral border)
Long head of biceps on the supraglenoid tubercle
Long head of triceps on the infraglenoid tubercle
Short head of biceps, coracobrachialis and pectoralis minor on the coracoid process
Trapezius and deltoid on the spine and acromion
Levator scapulae, rhomboid minor and rhomboid major on the medial border
Serratus anterior on the front of the medial border
Teres major on the back of the inferior angle
card.ossification: Body begins ossifying about week 8 of fetal life. Other centers (coracoid, acromion, glenoid) appear after birth and fuse by about age 20 to 25.
card.clinical: Injury to the long thoracic nerve paralyzes serratus anterior. The medial border then lifts off the rib cage (winged scapula).
card.quiz: Flat triangular bone with a spine, an acromion and a hook-like coracoid process.

parts.label: Trapezium bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Trapezium
card.summary: The four-sided carpal bone on the thumb side of the distal row. It forms the saddle joint at the base of the thumb.
landmarks: Groove for flexor carpi radialis tendon
attachments: Flexor retinaculum on the tubercle
Abductor pollicis brevis
Opponens pollicis
Flexor pollicis brevis
Radial collateral ligament of the wrist
card.ossification: Begins ossifying at about age 4 to 6 years.
card.clinical: Osteoarthritis of the thumb carpometacarpal joint is very common. It causes pain at the base of the thumb when pinching or gripping.
card.quiz: Carpal with a saddle-shaped facet for the thumb metacarpal.

parts.label: Trapezoid bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Trapezoid
card.summary: The smallest carpal bone of the distal row. It is wedge-shaped and sits in front of the base of the index metacarpal.
attachments: Carpal and carpometacarpal ligaments only
No muscles attach
card.ossification: Begins ossifying at about age 4 to 6 years.
card.clinical: It is rarely injured because it is wedged tightly between its neighbors. When it dislocates, it usually moves toward the back of the hand.
card.quiz: Smallest distal-row carpal; articulates with the index metacarpal.

parts.label: Triquetrum bone
parts.group: Bones of free part of upper limb.g > Bones of hand.g > Carpal bones.g

card.name: Triquetrum
card.summary: The pyramid-shaped carpal bone on the little-finger side of the proximal row. It carries the pisiform on its palmar surface.
articulations: Articular disc of the wrist (ulnocarpal side)
attachments: Ulnar collateral ligament of the wrist
Lunotriquetral interosseous ligament
Pisotriquetral ligaments
Palmar and dorsal radiocarpal ligaments
card.ossification: Begins ossifying at about age 2 to 3 years.
card.clinical: A small chip fracture on the back of the bone is the second most common carpal fracture. It follows a fall on the outstretched hand.
card.quiz: Pyramid-shaped carpal that articulates with the pisiform on its palmar side.

parts.label: Ulna
parts.group: Skeletal system.g > Bones of upper limb.g > Bones of free part of upper limb.g

card.name: Ulna
card.summary: The medial forearm bone, on the little-finger side. It is large at the elbow and forms the hinge with the humerus.
articulations: Humerus (humeroulnar joint, trochlear notch around trochlea)
Radius (distal radioulnar joint, ulnar head in ulnar notch)
Articular disc of the wrist (the ulna does not touch the carpal bones directly)
attachments: Triceps brachii on the olecranon
Brachialis on the ulnar tuberosity
Anconeus on the lateral olecranon and upper posterior shaft
Supinator on the supinator crest
Flexor digitorum profundus on the front and medial shaft
Pronator quadratus on the lower front of the shaft
Flexor carpi ulnaris on the olecranon and posterior border
Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis on the back of the shaft
Ulnar collateral ligament of the elbow on the coronoid process and olecranon
Annular ligament on the edges of the radial notch
card.ossification: Shaft ossifies before birth. The olecranon fuses at about age 16, and the distal end by about age 20.
card.clinical: An olecranon fracture is common after a fall on the elbow. The triceps can pull the broken piece upward. A broken ulnar shaft with a dislocated radial head is a Monteggia fracture.
card.quiz: Forearm bone on the little-finger side with a hook-like olecranon at the elbow.

parts.label: Abdominal part of pectoralis major muscle
parts.group: Thoracic part of muscular system.g > Muscles of thorax.g > Pectoralis major muscle.g

card.name: Pectoralis Major — Abdominal Part
card.summary: The lowest slip of the pectoralis major. It pulls the raised arm down and forward.
card.origin: Aponeurosis of the external oblique muscle (anterior layer of the rectus sheath)
card.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus. The lowest fibers fold under the others to reach it.
action: Depresses the raised arm against resistance
blood: Pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial artery
Perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery
card.clinical: The twisted tendon can rupture during bench pressing. Poland syndrome is a birth defect in which the sternocostal and abdominal parts are absent.
card.quiz: Lowest fibers of the big chest muscle. They arise from the abdominal wall and pull the raised arm down.

parts.label: Abductor digiti minimi of hand
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi (Hand)
card.summary: The outermost muscle of the little finger side of the palm. It spreads the little finger away from the ring finger.
card.clinical: Wasting flattens the little finger side of the palm in ulnar nerve palsy. Wartenberg sign is an abducted little finger that cannot be adducted.
card.quiz: Spreads the little finger away from the ring finger.
card.origin: Pisiform bone and the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris
card.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger, and the extensor expansion
action: Weakly flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint

parts.label: Abductor pollicis brevis
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Abductor Pollicis Brevis
card.summary: A thenar muscle on the outer edge of the palm. It moves the thumb straight forward, away from the palm.
card.clinical: Weakness and thenar wasting occur in severe carpal tunnel syndrome. Test by lifting the thumb straight up from a flat palm.
card.quiz: Lifts the thumb straight up from the palm, supplied by the recurrent median nerve.
card.origin: Flexor retinaculum, and the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium
card.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
action: Helps with opposition of the thumb
blood: Superficial palmar branch of radial artery

parts.label: Abductor pollicis longus
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Abductor Pollicis Longus
card.summary: A deep muscle on the back of the forearm. Its tendon runs to the base of the thumb and pulls the thumb away from the hand.
card.clinical: Its tendon and the extensor pollicis brevis tendon are involved in de Quervain tenosynovitis. This causes pain at the radial side of the wrist.
card.quiz: Forms the radial border of the anatomical snuffbox with extensor pollicis brevis.
card.origin: Posterior surfaces of the ulna and radius, and the interosseous membrane
card.insertion: Lateral side of the base of the first metacarpal
action: Abducts the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint
Extends the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Acromial part of deltoid muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Deltoid muscle.g

card.name: Deltoid — Middle (Acromial) Part
card.summary: The middle part of the deltoid. It is the main muscle that lifts the arm out to the side.
card.origin: Lateral margin of the acromion
card.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
action: Abducts the arm at the shoulder (about 15°–90°)
blood: Deltoid branch of the thoraco-acromial artery
card.clinical: The axillary nerve can be injured in a surgical neck fracture or shoulder dislocation. The shoulder then looks flat and the skin over it is numb.
card.quiz: Lifts the arm sideways from 15° to 90°.

parts.label: Anconeus muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Anconeus
card.summary: A small triangular muscle behind the elbow. It helps the triceps straighten the elbow and steadies the joint.
card.clinical: Pain over the lateral elbow can arise here, so it is part of the differential for tennis elbow. It also tenses the elbow joint capsule.
card.quiz: Small triangular muscle behind the elbow that assists the triceps.
card.origin: Posterior surface of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus
card.insertion: Lateral surface of the olecranon and the upper posterior surface of the ulna
action: Assists triceps brachii in extending the elbow
Abducts the ulna during forearm pronation
card.nerve: Radial nerve (branch from the nerve to the medial head of triceps)

parts.label: Ascending part of trapezius muscle
parts.group: Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g > Trapezius muscle.g

card.name: Trapezius — Lower (Ascending) Part
card.summary: The lower fibers of the trapezius. They pull the shoulder blade down and help turn it upward.
card.origin: Spinous processes of vertebrae T4–T12 (some texts: T3–T12)
card.insertion: Tubercle at the medial end of the spine of the scapula, through a small aponeurosis
action: Rotates the scapula upward (with the upper part and serratus anterior)
card.nerve: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with C3–C4 proprioceptive fibers
blood: Dorsal scapular artery (deep branch of the transverse cervical artery)
card.clinical: Weak lower trapezius is common with poor shoulder posture. Damage to CN XI weakens the whole muscle and causes a drooping shoulder.
card.quiz: Lowest fibers of the large kite-shaped upper back muscle. They pull the shoulder blade down.

parts.label: Brachialis muscle
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of arm.g

card.name: Brachialis
card.summary: A thick muscle under the biceps. It is the main muscle that bends the elbow.
card.origin: Distal half of the anterior surface of the humerus, and the intermuscular septa
card.insertion: Tuberosity of the ulna and the coronoid process of the ulna
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow in all positions (forearm pronated, supinated or neutral)
card.nerve: Musculocutaneous nerve (small lateral part: radial nerve)
blood: Muscular branches of the brachial artery
card.clinical: Called the workhorse of elbow flexion. Bone may form in it after elbow injury (myositis ossificans), which limits movement.
card.quiz: Deep muscle on the front of the lower humerus that bends the elbow whatever the forearm position.

parts.label: Brachioradialis muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Brachioradialis
card.summary: The muscle that forms the rounded outer bulge of the upper forearm. It flexes the elbow, most strongly when the thumb points up.
card.clinical: It is supplied by the radial nerve but flexes the elbow. The brachioradialis reflex tests C5 and C6.
card.quiz: Radial nerve muscle that flexes the elbow with the thumb pointing up.
card.origin: Proximal two thirds of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
card.insertion: Lateral surface of the distal radius, just above the styloid process
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow
Most effective with the forearm in mid-pronation
Returns the forearm toward mid-position from pronation or supination

parts.mesh: Clavicular head of pectoralis major muscle.r
parts.label: Clavicular head of pectoralis major muscle
parts.group: Thoracic part of muscular system.g > Muscles of thorax.g > Pectoralis major muscle.g

card.name: Pectoralis Major — Clavicular Head
card.summary: The upper part of the pectoralis major. It lifts the arm forward and turns it inward.
card.origin: Anterior surface of the medial half of the clavicle
card.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
action: Flexes the arm at the shoulder
blood: Pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial artery
card.clinical: This head works most in an incline press. It can still work when other parts of the muscle are absent or torn.
card.quiz: Upper fibers of the chest muscle that start from the collarbone and flex the arm.

parts.label: Clavicular part of deltoid muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Deltoid muscle.g

card.name: Deltoid — Front (Clavicular) Part
card.summary: The front part of the deltoid. It lifts the arm forward and turns it inward.
card.origin: Lateral third of the anterior border of the clavicle
card.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
action: Flexes the arm at the shoulder
blood: Deltoid branch of the thoraco-acromial artery
card.clinical: The front deltoid is often strained in overhead lifting. Axillary nerve injury weakens the whole deltoid.
card.quiz: Front fibers of the shoulder cap that raise the arm forward.

parts.label: Coracobrachialis muscle
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of arm.g

card.name: Coracobrachialis
card.summary: A small muscle on the upper inner arm. It flexes and adducts the arm. The musculocutaneous nerve passes through it.
card.origin: Tip of the coracoid process of the scapula (with the short head of biceps)
card.insertion: Middle third of the medial surface of the humerus
action: Flexes the arm at the shoulder
blood: Muscular branches of the brachial artery
card.clinical: The musculocutaneous nerve pierces this muscle. The muscle also serves as a guide to the axillary artery.
card.quiz: Small arm muscle that the musculocutaneous nerve pierces.

parts.mesh: Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis.r
parts.label: Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Flexor Pollicis Brevis — Deep Head
card.latin: Caput profundum musculi flexoris pollicis brevis
card.summary: The deeper part of flexor pollicis brevis. It joins the superficial head to bend the thumb at its base joint.
card.clinical: The deep head is usually ulnar-supplied, so flexor pollicis brevis can survive a median nerve injury. Some people vary from this pattern.
card.quiz: Thenar head supplied by the ulnar nerve, not the median.
card.origin: Trapezoid and capitate bones, and the palmar carpal ligaments
card.insertion: Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, with the superficial head
action: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint
blood: Superficial palmar branch of radial artery

parts.label: Deep head of pronator teres
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Pronator Teres — Deep (Ulnar) Head
card.summary: The small deep head of pronator teres. It joins the superficial head to turn the palm downward.
card.clinical: The median nerve passes between the two heads. Entrapment here causes pronator teres syndrome, with forearm pain and hand numbness.
card.quiz: Small head from the coronoid process; the median nerve passes between it and the other head.
card.origin: Medial side of the coronoid process of the ulna
card.insertion: Pronator tuberosity on the middle of the lateral surface of the radius, with the superficial head

parts.label: Descending part of trapezius muscle
parts.group: Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g > Trapezius muscle.g

card.name: Trapezius — Upper (Descending) Part
card.summary: The upper fibers of the trapezius. They lift the shoulder, as in a shrug, and move the neck.
card.origin: Medial third of the superior nuchal line, external occipital protuberance, nuchal ligament, and spinous process of C7
card.insertion: Lateral third of the clavicle
action: Extends and laterally flexes the neck; turns the face to the opposite side
card.nerve: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with C3–C4 proprioceptive fibers
blood: Superficial branch of the transverse cervical artery
card.clinical: Often tight and sore from desk work and stress. A weak shrug and a drooping shoulder suggest CN XI injury, for example after neck surgery.
card.quiz: Upper fibers of the large kite-shaped upper back muscle. They shrug the shoulder.

parts.label: Dorsal interossei muscles of hand
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Dorsal Interossei of the Hand
card.summary: Four small muscles between the metacarpals, each with two heads. They spread the fingers apart from the middle finger.
card.clinical: Ulnar nerve palsy causes weakness of finger spreading and hollowing between the metacarpals. Test by spreading the fingers against resistance.
card.quiz: Four bipennate muscles that spread the fingers; the memory aid is DAB.
card.origin: Adjacent sides of two neighboring metacarpals, with two heads each
card.insertion: Extensor expansions and bases of the proximal phalanges of digits 2 to 4
action: Abduct digits 2 to 4 away from the middle finger (DAB)
Extend the interphalangeal joints with the lumbricals
blood: Palmar metacarpal arteries (from deep palmar arch)

parts.label: Extensor carpi radialis brevis
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis
card.summary: A wrist extensor on the back of the forearm. It extends the wrist and tilts the hand toward the thumb side.
card.clinical: Its origin is the usual site of lateral epicondylitis, or tennis elbow. It often causes pain on the outer elbow when gripping.
card.quiz: Most often involved in tennis elbow; inserts on the third metacarpal.
card.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
card.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the third metacarpal
action: Fixes the wrist during finger flexion
card.nerve: Radial nerve (deep branch or posterior interosseous nerve)

parts.label: Extensor carpi radialis longus
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus
card.summary: A wrist extensor that lies beside brachioradialis. It extends the wrist and tilts the hand toward the thumb side.
card.clinical: It is spared in posterior interosseous nerve palsy. The wrist then extends weakly and deviates toward the thumb side.
card.quiz: Wrist extensor attaching to the second metacarpal, supplied before the radial nerve divides.
card.origin: Distal third of the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
card.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the second metacarpal

parts.label: Extensor digiti minimi
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Digiti Minimi
card.summary: A slender muscle that extends the little finger. It lets the little finger straighten independently.
card.clinical: It lets a person extend the little finger on its own, as when pointing the index and little finger. Its tendon passes in the fifth dorsal compartment.
card.quiz: Gives the little finger independent extension.
card.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
card.insertion: Extensor expansion of the little finger
action: Extends the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Extensor digitorum
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Digitorum
card.summary: The main muscle that straightens the four fingers. Its four tendons spread out over the back of the fingers.
card.clinical: Posterior interosseous nerve palsy causes finger drop, with the metacarpophalangeal joints unable to extend. Wrist extension is still possible.
card.quiz: Straightens the four fingers; weakness gives finger drop.
card.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
card.insertion: Extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5, reaching the middle and distal phalanges
action: Extends digits 2 to 5 at the metacarpophalangeal joints
Extends the interphalangeal joints with the interossei and lumbricals
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Extensor indicis
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Indicis
card.summary: A small deep muscle that extends the index finger. It allows the index finger to point on its own.
card.clinical: Surgeons often transfer this tendon to replace a ruptured extensor pollicis longus tendon. It is a convenient donor because extensor digitorum also extends the index finger.
card.quiz: Lets the index finger point alone; often used as a tendon transfer donor.
card.origin: Posterior surface of the ulna and the interosseous membrane, below the extensor pollicis longus
card.insertion: Extensor expansion of the index finger, joining the tendon of extensor digitorum
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Extensor pollicis brevis
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Pollicis Brevis
card.summary: A deep muscle whose tendon runs along the thumb. It straightens the first thumb joint and pulls the thumb outward.
card.clinical: Its tendon is involved in de Quervain tenosynovitis. A positive Finkelstein test causes sharp pain at the radial wrist.
card.quiz: Forms the radial border of the snuffbox and extends the first thumb joint.
card.origin: Posterior surface of the radius and the interosseous membrane, below abductor pollicis longus
card.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb
action: Extends the proximal phalanx of the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint
Extends and abducts the thumb at the carpometacarpal joint
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Extensor pollicis longus
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Pollicis Longus
card.summary: A deep muscle that straightens the thumb tip. Its tendon turns around Lister tubercle on the radius.
card.clinical: The tendon can rupture after a distal radius fracture or in rheumatoid arthritis. It forms the ulnar border of the anatomical snuffbox.
card.quiz: Its tendon turns around Lister tubercle and forms the snuffbox ulnar border.
card.origin: Lateral part of the middle third of the posterior ulna and the interosseous membrane
card.insertion: Dorsal surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
action: Extends the distal phalanx of the thumb
Extends the proximal phalanx and the carpometacarpal joint
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Flexor carpi radialis
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Carpi Radialis
card.summary: A superficial forearm muscle. Its tendon is easily felt at the front of the wrist, beside the radial artery pulse.
card.clinical: The radial artery pulse is felt just lateral to its tendon. The tendon is also a landmark for wrist surgery approaches.
card.quiz: Its wrist tendon sits beside the radial pulse.
card.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon)
card.insertion: Palmar surfaces of the bases of the second and third metacarpals

parts.label: Flexor digiti minimi of hand
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis (Hand)
card.latin: Musculus flexor digiti minimi brevis manus
card.summary: A small muscle on the little finger side of the palm. It bends the little finger at its base.
card.clinical: It weakens with ulnar nerve injury at the wrist or elbow. Its origin is near the hook of the hamate, which is a fracture site.
card.quiz: Bends the base of the little finger; arises from the hook of the hamate.
card.origin: Hook of the hamate and the flexor retinaculum
card.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger
action: Flexes the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint

parts.label: Flexor digitorum profundus
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Digitorum Profundus
card.summary: The deep finger flexor. It is the only muscle that bends the fingertip joints of digits 2 to 5.
card.clinical: Jersey finger is a rupture of its tendon from the distal phalanx, usually the ring finger. The fingertip cannot flex.
card.quiz: Only muscle that flexes the fingertip joints; split nerve supply (median and ulnar).
card.origin: Proximal three quarters of the medial and anterior surfaces of the ulna, and the interosseous membrane
card.insertion: Palmar surfaces of the bases of the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5
action: Flexes the distal interphalangeal joints of digits 2 to 5
Assists flexion of the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpophalangeal joints
card.nerve: Dual supply: median nerve (anterior interosseous branch) to digits 2 and 3; ulnar nerve to digits 4 and 5

parts.label: Flexor digitorum superficialis
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis
card.summary: A superficial finger flexor. It bends the middle joints of the four fingers, and its tendons split to let deep tendons pass.
card.clinical: Each tendon splits into two slips so the flexor digitorum profundus tendon can pass through. Test it by holding the other fingers straight.
card.quiz: Bends the middle joint of the fingers; its tendons split around the deep tendons.
card.origin: Humeroulnar head: medial epicondyle, ulnar collateral ligament and coronoid process. Radial head: anterior oblique line of the radius
card.insertion: Sides of the shafts of the middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5
action: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of digits 2 to 5

parts.label: Flexor pollicis longus
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Pollicis Longus
card.summary: A deep forearm muscle for the thumb. It is the only muscle that bends the tip of the thumb.
card.clinical: Anterior interosseous nerve palsy prevents making an OK sign. The thumb and index fingertips cannot pinch together.
card.quiz: Bends the thumb tip; weakness prevents the OK sign.
card.origin: Anterior surface of the radius and the adjacent interosseous membrane
card.insertion: Palmar surface of the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb
action: Flexes the interphalangeal joint of the thumb
Flexes the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb

parts.mesh: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris.r
parts.label: Humeral head of extensor carpi ulnaris
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris — Humeral Head
card.latin: Caput humerale musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris
card.summary: The upper head of extensor carpi ulnaris. It extends the wrist and tilts the hand toward the little finger side.
card.clinical: Tendon problems cause pain on the ulnar side of the wrist. It is often affected in racket sports and golf.
card.quiz: Common extensor origin head that tilts the wrist toward the little finger.
card.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus (common extensor tendon)
card.insertion: Medial side of the base of the fifth metacarpal, shared with the ulnar head
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.mesh: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
parts.label: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris — Humeral Head
card.latin: Caput humerale musculi flexoris carpi ulnaris
card.summary: The humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris. It flexes the wrist and tilts the hand toward the little finger side.
card.clinical: The ulnar nerve passes between the humeral and ulnar heads. Compression here is part of cubital tunnel syndrome.
card.quiz: Head from the medial epicondyle; the ulnar nerve passes beneath the two heads.
card.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon)
card.insertion: Pisiform, hook of the hamate and the base of the fifth metacarpal (via the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments)

parts.label: Infraspinatus muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Rotator cuff muscle.g

card.name: Infraspinatus
card.summary: A rotator cuff muscle on the back of the scapula. It turns the arm outward and holds the humeral head in its socket.
card.origin: Infraspinous fossa of the scapula
card.insertion: Middle facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
action: Stabilizes the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity
card.clinical: Tears are common in older adults. The suprascapular nerve can be trapped at the spinoglenoid notch, which wastes this muscle only.
card.quiz: Rotator cuff muscle below the scapular spine that rotates the arm outward.

parts.label: Lateral head of triceps brachii
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of arm.g > Triceps brachii muscle.g

card.name: Triceps Brachii — Lateral Head
card.summary: The outer head of the triceps. It extends the elbow and covers the radial nerve in its groove.
card.origin: Posterior surface of the humerus above the radial groove, and the lateral intermuscular septum
card.insertion: Proximal end of the olecranon of the ulna, through the common triceps tendon
action: Extends the forearm at the elbow
card.clinical: A fracture of the humeral shaft at the radial groove can injure the radial nerve and cause wrist drop.
card.quiz: Outer head of the muscle that straightens the elbow. It lies over the radial groove.

parts.label: Latissimus dorsi muscle
parts.group: Muscular system.g > Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g

card.name: Latissimus Dorsi
card.group: Back muscles acting on the arm
card.summary: A broad muscle of the back. It pulls the raised arm down and back, as in climbing or rowing.
card.origin: Spinous processes of T7–T12, thoracolumbar fascia, posterior iliac crest, lower three or four ribs, and inferior angle of the scapula
card.insertion: Floor of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
blood: Posterior intercostal and lumbar arteries (lower part)
card.clinical: Surgeons use it as a muscle flap for breast reconstruction. Damage to the thoracodorsal nerve weakens climbing and pulling.
card.quiz: Largest back muscle of the arm, used in climbing and pull-ups.

parts.label: Levator scapulae
parts.group: Muscular system.g > Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g

card.name: Levator Scapulae
card.summary: A strap muscle at the side of the neck. It lifts the shoulder blade.
card.origin: Posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of C1–C4
card.insertion: Superior angle and upper medial border of the scapula, down to the root of the spine
action: Bends the neck to the same side (when the scapula is fixed)
card.nerve: Dorsal scapular nerve and cervical spinal nerves C3–C4
card.roots: C3, C4 (and C5 via the dorsal scapular nerve)
card.clinical: A tight levator scapulae often causes a stiff neck and pain at the top corner of the shoulder blade.
card.quiz: Lifts the scapula from the upper neck vertebrae.

parts.label: Long head of biceps brachii
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of arm.g > Biceps brachii muscle.g

card.name: Biceps Brachii — Long Head
card.summary: The outer head of the biceps. Its tendon runs through the shoulder joint and bends the elbow.
card.origin: Supraglenoid tubercle of the scapula and the glenoid labrum
card.insertion: Radial tuberosity, and the bicipital aponeurosis (shared with the short head)
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow
Weakly flexes the arm at the shoulder
Helps hold the humeral head in the glenoid cavity
blood: Muscular branches of the brachial artery
card.clinical: Tendon rupture causes a bulging "Popeye" muscle. Tendinitis in the intertubercular groove causes shoulder pain.
card.quiz: Head of the two-headed elbow flexor whose tendon passes inside the shoulder joint.

parts.label: Long head of triceps brachii
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of arm.g > Triceps brachii muscle.g

card.name: Triceps Brachii — Long Head
card.summary: The longest head of the triceps. It crosses both the shoulder and the elbow, so it extends both.
card.origin: Infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula
card.insertion: Proximal end of the olecranon of the ulna, through the common triceps tendon
action: Extends the forearm at the elbow
Extends the arm at the shoulder
Helps stop the humeral head from sliding downward
card.clinical: It forms a border of the quadrangular and triangular spaces. The triceps reflex mainly tests C7.
card.quiz: Head of the main elbow extensor that starts on the scapula below the glenoid.

parts.label: Lumbrical muscles of hand
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Lumbricals of the Hand
card.summary: Four worm-like muscles that arise from the deep flexor tendons. They bend the finger bases and straighten the finger tips.
card.clinical: Ulnar nerve injury paralyzes the third and fourth lumbricals. The ring and little fingers form a claw with hyperextended metacarpophalangeal joints.
card.quiz: Bend the knuckles and straighten the finger tips; split median and ulnar supply.
card.origin: Tendons of flexor digitorum profundus: first and second from the lateral sides of tendons 2 and 3; third and fourth from adjacent sides of tendons 3 to 5
card.insertion: Lateral side of the extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5
card.nerve: First and second: median nerve. Third and fourth: ulnar nerve (deep branch)

parts.label: Medial head of triceps brachii
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of arm.g > Triceps brachii muscle.g

card.name: Triceps Brachii — Medial Head
card.summary: The deep head of the triceps. It works in all elbow extension and is the main workhorse of the muscle.
card.origin: Posterior surface of the humerus below the radial groove, and both intermuscular septa
card.insertion: Proximal end of the olecranon of the ulna, through the common triceps tendon
action: Extends the forearm at the elbow
card.clinical: The radial nerve passes between the lateral and medial heads in the radial groove. Humeral shaft fractures here can cause wrist drop.
card.quiz: Deepest head of the main elbow extensor, arising below the radial groove.

parts.label: Oblique head of adductor pollicis
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Adductor Pollicis — Oblique Head
card.summary: The oblique head of the thumb adductor. It lies deep in the palm and pulls the thumb toward the palm.
card.clinical: Weakness causes Froment sign. The patient substitutes flexor pollicis longus and bends the thumb tip when gripping paper.
card.quiz: Deep thumb muscle head from the capitate and bases of metacarpals 2 and 3; pulls the thumb toward the palm.
card.origin: Bases of the second and third metacarpals, the capitate and adjacent carpal bones
card.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, through a sesamoid bone, with the transverse head

parts.mesh: Opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand.r
parts.label: Opponens digiti minimi muscle of hand
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Opponens Digiti Minimi
card.summary: A small hypothenar muscle. It draws the fifth metacarpal forward to cup the palm and bring the little finger toward the thumb.
card.clinical: It weakens with ulnar nerve injury, flattening the hand. The ability to cup the palm for carrying water is reduced.
card.quiz: Cups the palm by rotating the fifth metacarpal toward the thumb.
card.origin: Hook of the hamate and the flexor retinaculum
card.insertion: Medial border and adjacent palmar surface of the fifth metacarpal
action: Draws the fifth metacarpal forward and rotates it (opposition of the little finger)
Deepens the hollow of the palm

parts.label: Opponens pollicis muscle
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Opponens Pollicis
card.summary: A deep thenar muscle. It rotates the thumb across the palm so the thumb pad meets the fingertips.
card.clinical: Loss of opposition is a key sign of a median nerve injury at the wrist. The thumb stays flat beside the index finger (ape hand).
card.quiz: Brings the thumb pad to meet the little finger; lost in ape hand.
card.origin: Flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium
card.insertion: Lateral border and adjacent palmar surface of the first metacarpal
action: Opposes the thumb by drawing the first metacarpal across the palm and rotating it
blood: Superficial palmar branch of radial artery

parts.label: Palmar interossei muscles
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Palmar Interossei
card.summary: Three small muscles on the palm side between the metacarpals. They pull the index, ring and little fingers toward the middle finger.
card.clinical: Weakness lets the fingers drift apart when held together. Test by gripping a piece of paper between extended fingers.
card.quiz: Three muscles that bring the fingers together; the memory aid is PAD.
card.origin: Palmar surfaces of the second, fourth and fifth metacarpals (second on its ulnar side; fourth and fifth on their radial sides)
card.insertion: Extensor expansions and bases of the proximal phalanges of digits 2, 4 and 5
action: Adduct digits 2, 4 and 5 toward the middle finger (PAD)
Extend the interphalangeal joints with the lumbricals
blood: Palmar metacarpal arteries (from deep palmar arch)

parts.label: Palmaris longus muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Palmaris Longus
card.summary: A slender superficial forearm muscle with a long tendon. It tightens the palm and weakly flexes the wrist.
card.clinical: It is absent in about 15% of people on at least one side. Surgeons often use its tendon as a graft.
card.quiz: Absent in about one in seven people; tightens the palmar aponeurosis.
card.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon)
card.insertion: Distal half of the flexor retinaculum and the palmar aponeurosis

parts.label: Pectoralis minor muscle
parts.group: Muscular system.g > Thoracic part of muscular system.g > Muscles of thorax.g

card.name: Pectoralis Minor
card.summary: A thin triangular muscle under the pectoralis major. It pulls the shoulder blade forward and down.
card.origin: Outer surfaces of ribs 3–5, near the costal cartilages
card.insertion: Medial border and upper surface of the coracoid process of the scapula
action: Depresses the scapula (draws it forward and down)
Elevates ribs 3–5 in forced breathing, when the scapula is fixed
blood: Pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial artery
card.clinical: Its tendon crosses the axillary artery and brachial plexus. A tight muscle can compress them (pectoralis minor syndrome).
card.quiz: Deep chest muscle that attaches to the coracoid process.

parts.label: Pronator quadratus
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Pronator Quadratus
card.summary: A flat, square muscle just above the wrist on the front of the forearm. It turns the palm downward and binds the radius to the ulna.
card.clinical: It is the prime mover of pronation, with pronator teres helping against resistance. Anterior interosseous nerve palsy weakens pronation with the elbow flexed.
card.quiz: Square muscle just above the wrist that turns the palm down.
card.origin: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the ulna
card.insertion: Distal quarter of the anterior surface of the radius
action: Holds the distal radius and ulna together

parts.mesh: Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis.r
parts.label: Radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis — Radial Head
card.latin: Caput radiale musculi flexoris digitorum superficialis
card.summary: The radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis. It lies on the radius and joins the humeroulnar head to bend the finger middle joints.
card.clinical: The fibrous arch joining the heads of this muscle can compress the median nerve. Test the whole muscle by flexing one finger with the others held straight.
card.quiz: Head of the finger flexor that arises from the radius.
card.origin: Anterior oblique line of the radius
card.insertion: Sides of the shafts of the middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5, shared with the humeroulnar head
action: Flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints of digits 2 to 5

parts.label: Rhomboid major muscle
parts.group: Muscular system.g > Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g

card.name: Rhomboid Major
card.summary: A flat muscle between the spine and the shoulder blade. It pulls the scapula toward the spine.
card.origin: Spinous processes of T2–T5
card.insertion: Medial border of the scapula, from the root of the spine to the inferior angle
action: Holds the scapula against the chest wall
card.clinical: Weakness lets the medial border of the scapula lift away from the chest, so the scapula looks winged.
card.quiz: Pulls the shoulder blades together. Lower of the two diamond-shaped muscles.

parts.label: Rhomboid minor muscle
parts.group: Muscular system.g > Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g

card.name: Rhomboid Minor
card.summary: A small flat muscle above the rhomboid major. It pulls the shoulder blade toward the spine.
card.origin: Lower part of the nuchal ligament and spinous processes of C7–T1
card.insertion: Medial border of the scapula at the root of the spine
action: Holds the scapula against the chest wall
card.clinical: Strain can cause pain between the shoulder blades. The dorsal scapular nerve can be injured during neck surgery.
card.quiz: Upper and smaller of the two diamond-shaped muscles between the spine and scapula.

parts.mesh: Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle.r
parts.label: Scapular spinal part of deltoid muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Deltoid muscle.g

card.name: Deltoid — Back (Spinal) Part
card.summary: The back part of the deltoid. It pulls the arm backward and turns it outward.
card.origin: Lower lip of the crest of the spine of the scapula
card.insertion: Deltoid tuberosity of the humerus
action: Extends the arm at the shoulder
blood: Deltoid branch of the profunda brachii artery
card.clinical: Axillary nerve injury weakens this part along with the rest of the deltoid. The posterior deltoid is often tested in extension.
card.quiz: Back fibers of the shoulder cap that start from the scapular spine.

parts.label: Serratus anterior muscle
parts.group: Muscular system.g > Thoracic part of muscular system.g > Muscles of thorax.g

card.name: Serratus Anterior
card.summary: A broad muscle on the side of the chest. It pulls the shoulder blade forward and holds it against the ribs.
card.origin: External surfaces of the lateral parts of ribs 1–8 (some texts: 1–9)
card.insertion: Costal surface of the medial border of the scapula
action: Holds the scapula against the thoracic wall
card.clinical: Long thoracic nerve injury, for example in breast surgery, causes winged scapula and difficulty raising the arm above the head.
card.quiz: Muscle that pushes the shoulder blade forward in a punch. Its nerve injury causes winged scapula.

parts.label: Short head of biceps brachii
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of arm.g > Biceps brachii muscle.g

card.name: Biceps Brachii — Short Head
card.summary: The inner head of the biceps. It bends and turns the forearm.
card.origin: Tip of the coracoid process of the scapula (with the coracobrachialis)
card.insertion: Radial tuberosity, and the bicipital aponeurosis (shared with the long head)
action: Flexes the forearm at the elbow
Weakly flexes the arm at the shoulder
blood: Muscular branches of the brachial artery
card.clinical: The biceps reflex tests C5–C6. The common tendon can rupture at the radial tuberosity, which weakens supination.
card.quiz: Head of the two-headed elbow flexor that starts on the coracoid process.

parts.mesh: Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle.r
parts.label: Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle
parts.group: Thoracic part of muscular system.g > Muscles of thorax.g > Pectoralis major muscle.g

card.name: Pectoralis Major — Sternocostal Head
card.summary: The large middle part of the pectoralis major. It pulls the arm across the chest and turns it inward.
card.origin: Anterior surface of the sternum and the upper six costal cartilages
card.insertion: Lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
action: Extends the flexed arm to the side of the trunk
blood: Pectoral branch of the thoraco-acromial artery
Perforating branches of the internal thoracic artery
card.clinical: This head is missing in Poland syndrome. A tear at the humeral insertion is a known weightlifting injury.
card.quiz: Largest part of the chest muscle, from the breastbone and rib cartilages.

parts.label: Subscapularis muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Rotator cuff muscle.g

card.name: Subscapularis
card.summary: A rotator cuff muscle on the front of the scapula. It turns the arm inward and supports the front of the shoulder.
card.origin: Subscapular fossa of the scapula
card.insertion: Lesser tubercle of the humerus
action: Stabilizes the humeral head, especially at the front
card.clinical: The lift-off test and belly-press test check it. It may tear in anterior shoulder dislocation.
card.quiz: Rotator cuff muscle on the front of the scapula that rotates the arm inward.

parts.mesh: Superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis.r
parts.label: Superficial head of flexor pollicis brevis
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Flexor Pollicis Brevis — Superficial Head
card.latin: Caput superficiale musculi flexoris pollicis brevis
card.summary: The larger, outer head of flexor pollicis brevis. It bends the thumb at its base joint.
card.clinical: A recurrent branch injury from a palm laceration paralyzes the thenar muscles. The thumb then cannot oppose.
card.quiz: Thenar head supplied by the recurrent median nerve.
card.origin: Distal border of the flexor retinaculum and the tubercle of the trapezium
card.insertion: Radial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, through a sesamoid bone
action: Flexes the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint
blood: Superficial palmar branch of radial artery

parts.label: Superficial head of pronator teres
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Pronator Teres — Superficial (Humeral) Head
card.summary: The main head of pronator teres. It forms the medial edge of the cubital fossa and turns the palm downward.
card.clinical: The median nerve usually passes between the two heads. This is a site of pronator teres syndrome.
card.quiz: Forms the medial border of the cubital fossa and pronates the forearm.
card.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus (common flexor tendon) and the antebrachial fascia
card.insertion: Pronator tuberosity on the middle of the lateral surface of the radius

parts.label: Supinator
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Deep part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Supinator
card.summary: A deep muscle that wraps around the upper radius. It turns the palm upward.
card.clinical: The posterior interosseous nerve passes through it at the arcade of Frohse. Compression here causes finger drop with sparing of wrist extension.
card.quiz: The deep branch of the radial nerve passes through this muscle that turns the palm up.
card.origin: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus, radial collateral and annular ligaments, and the supinator fossa and crest of the ulna
card.insertion: Lateral, posterior and anterior surfaces of the proximal third of the radius
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.label: Supraspinatus muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Rotator cuff muscle.g

card.name: Supraspinatus
card.summary: A rotator cuff muscle above the scapular spine. It starts arm abduction and holds the humeral head in place.
card.origin: Supraspinous fossa of the scapula
card.insertion: Superior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
action: Stabilizes the head of the humerus in the glenoid cavity
card.clinical: It is the rotator cuff muscle most often torn. It can be pinched under the acromion (impingement). The empty can test checks it.
card.quiz: Starts lifting the arm sideways. Most commonly torn cuff muscle.

parts.label: Teres major muscle
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g

card.name: Teres Major
card.summary: A thick muscle on the lower back of the scapula. It pulls the arm down and turns it inward.
card.origin: Dorsal surface of the inferior angle of the scapula
card.insertion: Medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus of the humerus
card.clinical: Often called the little helper of the latissimus dorsi. It forms the lower border of the quadrangular and triangular spaces.
card.quiz: Helper of the latissimus dorsi. It is not part of the rotator cuff.

parts.label: Teres minor muscle
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Scapulohumeral muscles.g > Rotator cuff muscle.g

card.name: Teres Minor
card.summary: A small rotator cuff muscle on the back of the scapula. It turns the arm outward.
card.origin: Upper two-thirds of the dorsal surface of the lateral border of the scapula
card.insertion: Inferior facet of the greater tubercle of the humerus
card.clinical: The axillary nerve passes through the quadrangular space beside it. Injury to the nerve weakens this muscle and the deltoid.
card.quiz: Small rotator cuff muscle that works with the infraspinatus. It is supplied by the axillary nerve.

parts.label: Transverse head of adductor pollicis
parts.group: Muscular system of upper limb.g > Muscles of upper limb.g > Muscles of hand.g

card.name: Adductor Pollicis — Transverse Head
card.summary: The transverse head of the thumb adductor. It is a fan-shaped sheet deep in the palm that pulls the thumb toward the index finger.
card.clinical: Weakness causes Froment sign. The patient cannot hold paper between the thumb and index finger with a straight thumb.
card.quiz: Fan-shaped deep thumb muscle head arising from the third metacarpal shaft.
card.origin: Palmar surface of the shaft of the third metacarpal
card.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, through a sesamoid bone, with the oblique head

parts.label: Transverse part of trapezius muscle
parts.group: Dorsal part of muscular system.g > Hypaxial muscles of back.g > Trapezius muscle.g

card.name: Trapezius — Middle (Transverse) Part
card.summary: The middle fibers of the trapezius. They pull the shoulder blades together.
card.origin: Spinous processes of C7–T3 (some texts: C7–T4)
card.insertion: Medial margin of the acromion and the upper lip of the crest of the spine of the scapula
card.nerve: Spinal accessory nerve (CN XI), with C3–C4 proprioceptive fibers
blood: Superficial branch of the transverse cervical artery
card.clinical: Weakness reduces scapular retraction and can contribute to rounded shoulders. CN XI injury weakens the whole trapezius.
card.quiz: Horizontal fibers of the large kite-shaped upper back muscle that squeeze the shoulder blades together.

parts.mesh: Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris.r
parts.label: Ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Posterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of posterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Extensor Carpi Ulnaris — Ulnar Head
