card.latin: Caput ulnare musculi extensoris carpi ulnaris
card.summary: The smaller ulnar head of extensor carpi ulnaris. It joins the humeral head to extend the wrist toward the little finger side.
card.clinical: Tendon inflammation or instability causes pain on the ulnar side of the wrist. It can snap over the ulnar groove with rotation.
card.quiz: Head from the posterior border of the ulna; extends the wrist and tilts the hand toward the little finger.
card.origin: Posterior border of the ulna, through an aponeurosis
card.insertion: Medial side of the base of the fifth metacarpal, shared with the humeral head
card.nerve: Posterior interosseous nerve (deep branch of radial nerve)

parts.mesh: Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
parts.label: Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris
parts.group: Muscles of upper limb.g > Anterior compartment of forearm.g > Superficial part of anterior compartment of forearm.g

card.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris — Ulnar Head
card.latin: Caput ulnare musculi flexoris carpi ulnaris
card.summary: The ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris. It arises from the elbow and ulna and joins the humeral head to bend the wrist.
card.clinical: The ulnar nerve runs under the aponeurosis joining the two heads. This is the cubital tunnel, a site of nerve compression.
card.quiz: Head from the olecranon and ulna; the ulnar nerve passes beneath its aponeurosis.
card.origin: Medial margin of the olecranon and the posterior border of the ulna, through an aponeurosis
card.insertion: Pisiform, hook of the hamate and the base of the fifth metacarpal (via the pisohamate and pisometacarpal ligaments)

parts.mesh: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.r
parts.label: Anterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.r

card.name: Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve — Anterior Branch
card.latin: Ramus anterior nervi cutanei antebrachii medialis
card.summary: The larger of the two terminal branches of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve. It carries sensation from the front and inner side of the forearm.
card.from: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (medial cord of the brachial plexus)
card.course: It arises in the arm and passes in front of, or beside, the median cubital vein. It then runs down the anteromedial forearm toward the wrist.
card.sensory: Skin of the anteromedial (front and inner) forearm, down toward the wrist.
card.injury: Numbness or tingling of the inner front forearm. There is no muscle weakness.
card.clinical: Branches of this nerve lie close to the median cubital and basilic veins. They can be injured during blood draws or vein surgery, causing a patch of numb skin.
card.quiz: Sensory nerve of the inner front forearm that runs near the cubital veins.

parts.mesh: Anterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus.r
parts.label: Anterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g > Inferior trunk of brachial plexus.r

card.name: Inferior Trunk — Anterior Division
card.latin: Divisio anterior trunci inferioris plexus brachialis
card.parent: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The front half of the inferior trunk. It carries fibers for the flexor (front) muscles of the arm, forearm and hand.
card.from: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It forms behind the clavicle as the inferior trunk splits. It continues as the medial cord, which then gives off the ulnar nerve and other medial branches.
card.sensory: None (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Lower plexus injury (Klumpke palsy) causes weak finger flexion and small hand muscles, often with a claw hand.
card.clinical: Pressure from a cervical rib or a lung apex tumor can injure the inferior trunk and cause weakness of the small hand muscles.
card.quiz: Front branch of the lowest trunk. It alone becomes the medial cord.

parts.mesh: Anterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus.r
parts.label: Anterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g > Middle trunk of brachial plexus.r

card.name: Middle Trunk — Anterior Division
card.latin: Divisio anterior trunci medii plexus brachialis
card.parent: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The front half of the middle trunk. It carries C7 fibers for the flexor (front) side of the limb.
card.from: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It forms behind the clavicle. It joins the anterior division of the superior trunk to form the lateral cord.
card.sensory: None (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Isolated damage is rare. Its C7 fibers pass to the lateral cord and mainly the lateral root of the median nerve, so loss can weaken pronator teres and flexor carpi radialis.
card.clinical: Together with the superior trunk, it forms the lateral cord. That cord gives the musculocutaneous nerve and the lateral root of the median nerve.
card.quiz: Front branch of the C7 trunk. It joins the upper trunk to make the lateral cord.

parts.mesh: Anterior division of superior trunk of brachial plexus.r
parts.label: Anterior division of superior trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g > Superior trunk of brachial plexus.r

card.name: Superior Trunk — Anterior Division
card.latin: Divisio anterior trunci superioris plexus brachialis
card.parent: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The front half of the superior trunk. It carries C5 and C6 fibers for the flexor (front) side of the limb.
card.from: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It forms behind the clavicle. It joins the anterior division of the middle trunk to form the lateral cord.
card.sensory: None (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Upper plexus injury (Erb palsy) causes weak elbow flexion and an arm held at the side, turned inward.
card.clinical: Injury to the upper trunk (Erb palsy) weakens the biceps, brachialis and deltoid. The arm hangs by the side in the waiter-tip position.
card.quiz: Front branch of the upper trunk. It helps form the lateral cord.

parts.label: Anterior interosseous nerve of forearm
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Median nerve.r

card.name: Anterior Interosseous Nerve
card.summary: A deep motor branch of the median nerve in the forearm. It supplies the deep flexors of the thumb, index finger and middle finger, and the pronator quadratus.
card.from: Median nerve, in the upper forearm just below the elbow
card.course: It runs down the front of the interosseous membrane with the anterior interosseous artery, between flexor pollicis longus and flexor digitorum profundus. It ends deep to pronator quadratus.
motor: Flexor digitorum profundus (lateral half: index and middle fingers)
card.sensory: No skin supply. It sends fibers to the wrist joint for deep pain sense.
card.injury: Loss of flexion at the thumb tip and index fingertip. The patient cannot form an OK sign.
card.clinical: Anterior interosseous syndrome causes a weak pinch. The patient cannot make an OK sign because the thumb and index tips do not flex.
card.quiz: Deep forearm branch that runs on the interosseous membrane and ends at the wrist joint.

parts.label: Axillary nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Axillary Nerve
card.group: Terminal branches of the brachial plexus
card.summary: A terminal branch of the posterior cord. It supplies the deltoid and teres minor and the skin over the lower deltoid.
card.from: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It leaves the axilla through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery. It wraps around the surgical neck of the humerus under the deltoid.
card.sensory: Skin over the lower deltoid (regimental badge area), via the superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve. Also the shoulder joint capsule.
card.injury: Weak arm abduction beyond the first 15°, a flattened shoulder, and numbness over the lower deltoid.
card.clinical: It is injured by surgical neck fractures, anterior shoulder dislocation, or poorly fitted crutches. The deltoid wastes and the round shoulder contour is lost.
card.quiz: Winds around the surgical neck of the humerus and supplies the deltoid.

parts.mesh: Common palmar digital branches of median nerve.r
parts.label: Common palmar digital branches of median nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Median nerve.r

card.name: Median Nerve — Common Palmar Digital Branches
card.latin: Nervi digitales palmares communes nervi mediani
card.summary: The branches of the median nerve in the palm. Each divides near a finger web into proper palmar digital nerves.
card.from: Median nerve, after it leaves the carpal tunnel
card.course: Three branches run toward the thumb web, the second web and the third web. Each splits into proper palmar digital nerves for adjacent digits.
card.sensory: Palmar skin of the thumb, index finger, middle finger and the lateral half of the ring finger, with their nail beds.
card.injury: Numbness of the lateral three and a half fingers, and weak index and middle finger lumbricals.
card.clinical: Carpal tunnel syndrome compresses the median nerve before these branches arise. It causes numbness and tingling in the lateral three and a half fingers.
card.quiz: Palm branches that fan out to the first three finger webs.

parts.mesh: Common palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve.r
parts.label: Common palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r > Superficial branch of ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Common Palmar Digital Branches
card.latin: Nervi digitales palmares communes nervi ulnaris
card.summary: A palm branch of the superficial ulnar nerve. It runs to the fourth finger web and splits into proper digital nerves.
card.from: Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve
card.course: It runs toward the web between the ring and little fingers. There it divides into proper palmar digital nerves.
card.sensory: Palmar skin of the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.
card.injury: Numbness of the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.
card.clinical: A lesion of the ulnar nerve at the wrist or elbow numbs the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.
card.quiz: Palm branch to the fourth web space on the medial side of the hand.

parts.mesh: Communicating branch of median nerve with ulnar nerve.r
parts.label: Communicating branch of median nerve with ulnar nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Median nerve.r

card.name: Median Nerve — Communicating Branch to Ulnar Nerve
card.summary: A small connecting branch between the median nerve and the ulnar nerve. Most often it lies in the palm and links their digital branches.
card.from: Median nerve (third common palmar digital nerve)
card.course: In the palm it crosses to join the ulnar common palmar digital nerve to the fourth web. A forearm version (Martin–Gruber) also occurs in some people.
card.sensory: Mixed sensory fibers that overlap the ring finger skin supplied by both nerves.
card.clinical: This link explains why some people have unusual sensation or muscle weakness patterns after median or ulnar nerve injury.
card.quiz: Small palm connection between the two nerves that share the ring finger.

parts.label: Deep branch of radial nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r

card.name: Radial Nerve — Deep Branch
card.summary: The motor branch of the radial nerve in the forearm. It supplies the supinator and then continues as the posterior interosseous nerve.
card.from: Radial nerve, in front of the lateral epicondyle
card.course: It winds around the radius through the supinator muscle. After the muscle it continues as the posterior interosseous nerve.
motor: Then continues as the posterior interosseous nerve to the finger and thumb extensors
card.sensory: No skin supply. Small branches go to the wrist joint.
card.injury: Finger drop with the wrist still able to extend weakly toward the thumb side.
card.clinical: The nerve passes through a tendinous arch of the supinator (arcade of Frohse). Compression there can cause weak finger extension.
card.quiz: Motor branch that pierces the supinator and then becomes the posterior interosseous nerve.

parts.label: Deep branch of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Deep Branch
card.summary: The motor branch of the ulnar nerve in the hand. It supplies most of the small intrinsic muscles of the hand.
card.from: Ulnar nerve, near the pisiform bone
card.course: It passes between the hypothenar muscles and curves around the hook of the hamate. It then crosses the palm with the deep palmar arch.
card.sensory: None (motor only), apart from small branches to wrist joints.
card.injury: Clawing of the ring and little fingers, weak finger spreading, and weak pinch (Froment sign).
card.clinical: Compression in Guyon canal, for example from handlebars (cyclist palsy), weakens the hand muscles but leaves skin sensation normal.
card.quiz: Deep palm motor nerve that curves around the hook of the hamate.

parts.label: Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Dorsal Branch
card.summary: A sensory branch of the ulnar nerve. It supplies the back of the medial hand and the back of the little finger and half of the ring finger.
card.from: Ulnar nerve, about 5 cm above the wrist
card.course: It passes deep to flexor carpi ulnaris and winds to the back of the wrist. It then divides into dorsal digital nerves.
card.sensory: Skin of the medial dorsum of the hand and the dorsal little finger and medial half of the ring finger.
card.injury: Numbness of the back of the medial hand and the little finger.
card.clinical: Numbness on the back of the medial hand suggests a lesion proximal to the wrist. A lesion in Guyon canal spares this area.
card.quiz: Leaves the main nerve about 5 cm above the wrist and winds under flexor carpi ulnaris to the back of the hand.

parts.mesh: Dorsal digital branches of radial nerve.r
parts.label: Dorsal digital branches of radial nerve
parts.group: Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r > Superficial branch of radial nerve.r

card.name: Radial Nerve — Dorsal Digital Branches
card.summary: The terminal sensory twigs of the superficial radial nerve. They supply the skin on the back of the thumb and lateral fingers.
card.from: Superficial branch of the radial nerve
card.course: They arise on the back of the hand. They run along the sides of the thumb, index finger, middle finger and radial half of the ring finger.
card.sensory: Skin on the back of the thumb and the proximal parts of the index finger, middle finger and lateral ring finger.
card.injury: Numbness on the back of the thumb and index finger web, without muscle weakness.
card.clinical: The skin of the first dorsal web space is the radial nerve autonomous zone. It is the usual place to test radial sensation.
card.quiz: Back-of-hand sensory twigs for the thumb and the next two and a half fingers.

parts.mesh: Dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve.r
parts.label: Dorsal digital branches of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r > Dorsal branch of ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Dorsal Digital Branches
card.summary: The terminal twigs of the dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve. They supply skin on the back of the little finger and half of the ring finger.
card.from: Dorsal branch of the ulnar nerve
card.course: They run along the back of the medial hand toward the little finger and ring finger. They supply the skin as far as the proximal finger joints.
card.sensory: Skin on the back of the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger, proximal to the nail beds.
card.injury: Numbness on the back of the little finger and ring finger.
card.clinical: The nail bed area is supplied by palmar digital nerves instead, so the fingertip may keep feeling when the dorsal branch is cut.
card.quiz: Back-of-hand twigs for the little finger and half of the ring finger.

parts.label: Dorsal scapular nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular branches of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Dorsal Scapular Nerve
card.group: Branches from the roots of the brachial plexus
card.summary: A small nerve from the C5 root. It supplies the rhomboid muscles that pull the scapula toward the spine.
card.from: Root C5 of the brachial plexus
card.course: It pierces the middle scalene muscle and runs deep to levator scapulae. It then runs along the medial border of the scapula under the rhomboids.
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Weak scapular retraction and slight winging of the scapula.
card.clinical: Entrapment as it crosses the middle scalene can cause deep, dull pain along the medial border of the scapula.
card.quiz: Branch of the C5 root that supplies the rhomboids.

parts.label: Inferior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r

card.name: Inferior Lateral Brachial Cutaneous Nerve
card.group: Cutaneous branches of the radial nerve
card.summary: A sensory branch of the radial nerve. It supplies skin on the lower outer part of the arm.
card.from: Radial nerve, in or near the spiral groove
card.course: It pierces the lateral head of triceps and the deep fascia. It then runs down the lateral arm to the elbow.
card.sensory: Skin of the lower lateral arm, down to the elbow.
card.injury: Numb patch over the lower outer arm.
card.clinical: It can be damaged along with the radial nerve in a humeral shaft fracture, causing a numb patch on the outer arm.
card.quiz: Skin nerve of the lower outer arm that comes from the radial nerve.

parts.label: Inferior trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Inferior Trunk of the Brachial Plexus
card.summary: The lowest trunk of the brachial plexus. It is formed by the C8 and T1 ventral rami.
card.from: Union of the ventral rami of C8 and T1
card.course: It arches over the first rib behind the subclavian artery. Behind the clavicle it divides into anterior and posterior divisions.
card.sensory: None directly (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Klumpke palsy: weak hand muscles with a claw hand and numbness on the inner arm and forearm.
card.clinical: Pressure from a cervical rib or a lung apex tumor (Pancoast tumor) can injure it. T1 involvement may also cause Horner syndrome.
card.quiz: Lowest trunk, formed by C8 and T1.

parts.label: Lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of lateral cord of brachial plexus.g > Musculocutaneous nerve.r

card.name: Lateral Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve
card.summary: The continuation of the musculocutaneous nerve below the elbow. It is a skin nerve for the outer forearm.
card.from: Musculocutaneous nerve (lateral cord of the brachial plexus)
card.course: It emerges lateral to the biceps tendon and pierces the deep fascia. It then runs with the cephalic vein down the lateral forearm to the wrist.
card.sensory: Skin of the lateral (thumb side) forearm, reaching the base of the thenar eminence.
card.injury: Numbness over the lateral forearm. There is no weakness.
card.clinical: It can be injured during biceps tendon repair or radial artery puncture, causing numbness on the thumb side of the forearm.
card.quiz: Continuation of the musculocutaneous nerve. It supplies the outer forearm skin.

parts.label: Lateral pectoral nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of lateral cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Lateral Pectoral Nerve
card.summary: A branch of the lateral cord. It mainly supplies the pectoralis major muscle on the chest.
card.from: Lateral cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It crosses in front of the axillary artery and pierces the clavipectoral fascia. It supplies pectoralis major and joins a loop with the medial pectoral nerve.
motor: Pectoralis minor (through the loop with the medial pectoral nerve)
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Weak arm adduction and inward rotation.
card.clinical: It can be injured during breast or axillary surgery. Weakness of the pectoral muscles is then noticed when pushing or adducting the arm.
card.quiz: Chest nerve from the lateral cord. It supplies the main chest muscle.

parts.label: Long thoracic nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular branches of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Long Thoracic Nerve
card.group: Branches from the roots of the brachial plexus
card.summary: A motor nerve to the serratus anterior muscle. It arises from the roots of the plexus and runs down the side of the chest.
card.from: Roots C5, C6 and C7 of the brachial plexus
card.course: It pierces the middle scalene and passes behind the plexus. It then descends on the outer surface of serratus anterior along the midaxillary line.
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Winged scapula, and difficulty raising the arm above horizontal.
card.clinical: It lies on the side of the chest wall and is easily hurt in breast surgery or axillary node dissection. Injury causes a winged scapula.
card.quiz: Runs down the lateral chest wall to the muscle that holds the scapula flat.

parts.label: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve
card.summary: A skin nerve from the medial cord. It supplies the inner side of the forearm.
card.from: Medial cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It runs down the arm medial to the brachial artery. It pierces the deep fascia with the basilic vein and splits into anterior and posterior branches.
card.sensory: Skin of the medial (little finger side) forearm.
card.injury: Numbness of the medial forearm. There is no weakness.
card.clinical: It lies close to the basilic vein and can be injured during vein surgery. The result is numbness on the inner forearm.
card.quiz: Skin nerve of the inner forearm that arises from the medial cord.

parts.label: Medial brachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Medial Brachial Cutaneous Nerve
card.summary: A small sensory branch of the medial cord. It supplies skin on the inner side of the arm.
card.from: Medial cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It runs down the medial arm and joins the intercostobrachial nerve (T2) in the axilla. It pierces the deep fascia in the lower arm.
card.sensory: Skin of the medial arm, reaching as far as the medial epicondyle.
card.injury: Numb patch on the inner arm.
card.clinical: Numbness here after axillary surgery usually involves the neighboring intercostobrachial nerve as well.
card.quiz: Skin nerve of the inner arm.

parts.label: Median nerve
parts.group: Peripheral nervous system.g > Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g

card.name: Median Nerve
card.group: Terminal branches of the brachial plexus
card.summary: A main nerve of the front of the forearm and hand. It flexes the wrist and fingers, pronates the forearm, and moves the thumb.
card.from: Lateral and medial cords of the brachial plexus (two roots that join around the axillary artery)
card.course: It runs down the arm beside the brachial artery and passes through the cubital fossa. It then runs between flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus and through the carpal tunnel.
motor: Forearm: pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor digitorum superficialis
Anterior interosseous branch: flexor pollicis longus, lateral half of flexor digitorum profundus, pronator quadratus
Hand: abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis (superficial head), first and second lumbricals
card.sensory: Palmar skin of the lateral three and a half digits and the lateral palm. Also the fingertip skin on the back of the index, middle and ring fingers.
card.injury: At the wrist: ape hand and weak thumb opposition. High lesion: hand of benediction when making a fist.
card.clinical: Carpal tunnel syndrome compresses it at the wrist. It causes night-time tingling and weak thumb opposition.
card.quiz: Nerve of the carpal tunnel. It supplies the thumb muscles and the lateral three and a half fingers.

parts.label: Middle trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Middle Trunk of the Brachial Plexus
card.summary: The middle trunk of the brachial plexus. It is the continuation of the C7 ventral ramus.
card.from: Ventral ramus of C7
card.course: It passes laterally across the posterior triangle of the neck. Behind the clavicle it divides into anterior and posterior divisions.
card.sensory: None directly (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Weak elbow, wrist and finger extension, and possible numbness of the middle finger.
card.clinical: Isolated injury is rare. Damage to C7 weakens extension of the elbow, wrist and fingers.
card.quiz: The only trunk made from a single root: C7.

parts.label: Muscular branches of axillary nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Axillary nerve.r

card.name: Axillary Nerve — Muscular Branches
card.summary: The motor branches of the axillary nerve. They supply the deltoid and the teres minor.
card.from: Axillary nerve (posterior cord of the brachial plexus)
card.course: An anterior branch winds around the surgical neck to the deltoid. A posterior branch supplies teres minor and the back of the deltoid.
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Weak abduction of the arm beyond the first 15° and weak outward rotation.
card.clinical: These branches are at risk in surgical neck fractures and anterior dislocations. The deltoid then wastes and the shoulder looks flattened.
card.quiz: Motor twigs to the deltoid and teres minor.

parts.label: Muscular branches of median nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Median nerve.r

card.name: Median Nerve — Muscular Branches
card.summary: The motor branches of the median nerve to the front of the forearm. A recurrent branch in the hand supplies the thenar muscles.
card.from: Median nerve
card.course: Branches leave near the elbow to the pronator and superficial flexors. The recurrent branch loops back at the lower edge of the flexor retinaculum to the thenar muscles.
motor: Thenar muscles: abductor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis, flexor pollicis brevis (superficial head)
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Weak pronation and wrist flexion. Wasting of the thenar muscles and loss of thumb opposition.
card.clinical: The recurrent thenar branch lies just under the skin of the palm. A shallow cut there can paralyze the thumb muscles.
card.quiz: Direct motor twigs to the superficial forearm flexors and, via the recurrent branch, the thenar muscles.

parts.label: Muscular branches of radial nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r

card.name: Radial Nerve — Muscular Branches
card.summary: The motor branches of the radial nerve above the elbow. They supply the triceps, anconeus, brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus.
card.from: Radial nerve
card.course: The triceps branches leave in the axilla and spiral groove. Branches to brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus arise near the elbow.
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Wrist drop. High lesions in the axilla also weaken elbow extension.
card.clinical: A midshaft humeral fracture damages the nerve below the triceps branches. Triceps works, but the wrist and fingers cannot extend.
card.quiz: Motor twigs to the triceps, anconeus, brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus.

parts.label: Muscular branches of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Muscular Branches
card.summary: The motor branches of the ulnar nerve in the forearm. They supply flexor carpi ulnaris and half of flexor digitorum profundus.
card.from: Ulnar nerve, just below the elbow
card.course: They arise after the nerve passes between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris. They enter flexor carpi ulnaris and the medial half of flexor digitorum profundus.
motor: Flexor digitorum profundus (medial half: ring and little fingers)
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: Weak wrist flexion with ulnar deviation, and weak ring and little finger tip flexion.
card.clinical: Compression at the cubital tunnel at the elbow can weaken grip and wrist flexion on the inner side.
card.quiz: Motor twigs in the forearm to the ulnar wrist flexor and the ring and little finger deep flexor.

parts.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of lateral cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Musculocutaneous Nerve
card.group: Terminal branches of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The nerve of the front compartment of the arm. It flexes the elbow and supplies the skin of the outer forearm.
card.from: Lateral cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It pierces coracobrachialis and runs between biceps brachii and brachialis. It then continues as the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.
card.sensory: Skin of the lateral forearm, through the lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerve.
card.injury: Weak elbow flexion and supination, loss of the biceps reflex, and numbness of the lateral forearm.
card.clinical: The biceps tendon reflex tests C5–C6 through this nerve. Isolated injury is uncommon and may follow shoulder dislocation.
card.quiz: Pierces coracobrachialis and supplies the flexors of the arm.

parts.label: Palmar branch of median nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Median nerve.r

card.name: Median Nerve — Palmar Cutaneous Branch
card.summary: A small skin branch of the median nerve. It supplies the base of the thumb and the center of the palm.
card.from: Median nerve, in the lower forearm, about 5 cm above the wrist
card.course: It passes over the flexor retinaculum rather than under it. It supplies the skin of the thenar eminence and the central palm.
card.sensory: Skin over the thenar eminence and the central palm.
card.injury: Numbness over the thenar eminence is not seen in carpal tunnel syndrome. It occurs with a lesion above the wrist.
card.clinical: Because it passes over the carpal tunnel, thenar skin sensation is spared in carpal tunnel syndrome.
card.quiz: Skin branch that goes over, not through, the carpal tunnel.

parts.label: Palmar branch of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Palmar Cutaneous Branch
card.summary: A small skin branch of the ulnar nerve. It supplies the skin of the medial palm.
card.from: Ulnar nerve, in the mid-forearm
card.course: It runs down in front of the ulnar artery and pierces the deep fascia near the wrist. It supplies the skin over the hypothenar eminence.
card.sensory: Skin of the medial palm over the hypothenar eminence.
card.injury: Numbness of the medial palm when the ulnar nerve is cut above mid-forearm.
card.clinical: It passes over Guyon canal, so palm skin sensation can remain even when the ulnar nerve is compressed at the canal.
card.quiz: Skin branch that runs over Guyon canal to the hypothenar part of the palm.

parts.label: Posterior antebrachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r

card.name: Posterior Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve
card.group: Cutaneous branches of the radial nerve
card.summary: A skin branch of the radial nerve. It supplies the back of the forearm.
card.from: Radial nerve, in the spiral groove of the humerus
card.course: It pierces the lateral head of triceps and runs down the back of the arm. It continues down the middle of the posterior forearm to the wrist.
card.sensory: Skin of the posterior forearm, from the elbow to the wrist.
card.injury: Numbness on the back of the forearm.
card.clinical: It is often spared in forearm-level radial nerve injuries because it branches off higher up the arm.
card.quiz: Skin nerve of the back of the forearm from the radial nerve.

parts.mesh: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.r
parts.label: Posterior branch of medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve.r

card.name: Medial Antebrachial Cutaneous Nerve — Posterior Branch
card.latin: Ramus posterior nervi cutanei antebrachii medialis
card.summary: The smaller terminal branch of the medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve. It supplies the back and inner side of the forearm.
card.from: Medial antebrachial cutaneous nerve (medial cord of the brachial plexus)
card.course: It passes in front of the medial epicondyle and runs down the medial and back side of the forearm to the wrist.
card.sensory: Skin of the posteromedial forearm.
card.injury: Numbness of the posteromedial forearm.
card.clinical: It passes near the medial epicondyle and can be hurt in elbow surgery, giving numbness of the inner forearm.
card.quiz: Back branch of the inner forearm skin nerve.

parts.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Infraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Posterior Cord of the Brachial Plexus
card.summary: The cord behind the axillary artery. It is formed by all three posterior divisions and supplies the extensor side of the upper limb.
card.from: Union of the posterior divisions of the superior, middle and inferior trunks
card.course: It lies behind the second part of the axillary artery. It gives the upper and lower subscapular nerves, thoracodorsal nerve, axillary nerve and radial nerve.
card.sensory: None directly (carried by its branches)
card.injury: Wrist drop, weak elbow extension and shoulder weakness, with numbness over the back of the arm and hand.
card.clinical: A crutch pressed into the axilla can injure it. This weakens shoulder abduction, and the elbow, wrist and finger extensors.
card.quiz: Cord behind the axillary artery that ends as the axillary and radial nerves.

parts.mesh: Posterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus.r
parts.label: Posterior division of inferior trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g > Inferior trunk of brachial plexus.r

card.name: Inferior Trunk — Posterior Division
card.latin: Divisio posterior trunci inferioris plexus brachialis
card.parent: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The back half of the inferior trunk. It carries C8 and T1 fibers for the extensor (back) side of the limb.
card.from: Inferior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It forms behind the clavicle. It joins the other two posterior divisions to form the posterior cord.
card.sensory: None (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Part of lower plexus injury, with weakness of the lowest radial nerve muscles.
card.clinical: Lower trunk injury can affect these fibers. This can weaken finger and thumb extensors supplied by the radial nerve.
card.quiz: Back branch of the lowest trunk. It feeds the posterior cord.

parts.mesh: Posterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus.r
parts.label: Posterior division of middle trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g > Middle trunk of brachial plexus.r

card.name: Middle Trunk — Posterior Division
card.latin: Divisio posterior trunci medii plexus brachialis
card.parent: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The back half of the middle trunk. It carries C7 fibers for the extensor (back) side of the limb.
card.from: Middle trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It forms behind the clavicle. It joins the other two posterior divisions to form the posterior cord.
card.sensory: None (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Part of a C7 injury, with weak elbow and wrist extension.
card.clinical: C7 contributes much of the power to the triceps and wrist extensors through the radial nerve.
card.quiz: Back branch of the C7 trunk that feeds the posterior cord.

parts.mesh: Posterior division of superior trunk of brachial plexus.r
parts.label: Posterior division of superior trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g > Superior trunk of brachial plexus.r

card.name: Superior Trunk — Posterior Division
card.latin: Divisio posterior trunci superioris plexus brachialis
card.parent: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The back half of the superior trunk. It carries C5 and C6 fibers for the extensor (back) side of the limb.
card.from: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It forms behind the clavicle. It joins the other two posterior divisions to form the posterior cord.
card.sensory: None (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Part of Erb palsy, with a weak deltoid and teres minor.
card.clinical: These fibers supply the deltoid, teres minor and brachioradialis through the axillary and radial nerves. Upper plexus injury weakens them.
card.quiz: Back branch of the upper trunk that feeds the posterior cord.

parts.label: Posterior interosseous nerve of forearm
parts.group: Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r > Deep branch of radial nerve.r

card.name: Posterior Interosseous Nerve
card.summary: The continuation of the deep radial nerve after the supinator. It supplies most of the extensor muscles on the back of the forearm.
card.from: Deep branch of the radial nerve
card.course: It emerges from the supinator and runs between the superficial and deep extensors. It lies on the interosseous membrane and ends at the wrist joint.
card.sensory: No skin supply. It carries deep pain and position sense from the wrist joint.
card.injury: Finger drop and weak thumb extension. Wrist extension remains but deviates toward the thumb side.
card.clinical: Compression at the arcade of Frohse or a Monteggia fracture can injure it. The result is finger drop with no wrist drop.
card.quiz: Deep radial nerve continuation that supplies the finger and thumb extensors.

parts.mesh: Proper palmar digital branches of median nerve.r
parts.label: Proper palmar digital branches of median nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Median nerve.r > Common palmar digital branches of median nerve.r

card.name: Median Nerve — Proper Palmar Digital Branches
card.latin: Nervi digitales palmares proprii nervi mediani
card.summary: The final sensory nerves of the median nerve to the digits. Each digit has one on each side.
card.from: Common palmar digital branches of the median nerve
card.course: They run along the sides of the thumb, index finger, middle finger and lateral ring finger. They also send twigs to the back of the fingertips.
card.sensory: Palmar skin of the thumb, index finger, middle finger and lateral half of the ring finger. Also the nail bed and fingertip skin on the dorsum.
card.injury: Fingertip numbness from cuts at the sides of the lateral three and a half fingers.
card.clinical: A digital nerve block at the base of the finger numbs the finger by anesthetizing these nerves on both sides.
card.quiz: Final finger-side sensory nerves to the lateral three and a half digits.

parts.mesh: Proper palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve.r
parts.label: Proper palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Ulnar nerve.r > Superficial branch of ulnar nerve.r > Common palmar digital branches of ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Proper Palmar Digital Branches
card.latin: Nervi digitales palmares proprii nervi ulnaris
card.summary: The final sensory nerves of the ulnar nerve to the little finger and half of the ring finger.
card.from: Superficial branch of the ulnar nerve (via the common palmar digital branch)
card.course: They run along the sides of the little finger and the medial side of the ring finger. They also send twigs to the back of the fingertips.
card.sensory: Palmar skin of the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger, with the fingertip skin on the dorsum.
card.injury: Numbness of the palmar little finger and medial half of the ring finger.
card.clinical: Ulnar nerve damage at the wrist or elbow causes numbness of the little finger. This is the best skin test for the ulnar nerve.
card.quiz: Final finger-side nerves for the little finger and half of the ring finger.

parts.label: Radial nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Radial Nerve
card.group: Terminal branches of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The largest branch of the brachial plexus. It supplies the extensor muscles of the arm, forearm and hand.
card.from: Posterior cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It runs behind the humerus in the spiral groove with the deep brachial artery. In front of the lateral epicondyle it divides into superficial and deep branches.
motor: Supinator and the forearm extensors, via the deep branch
card.sensory: Skin of the back of the arm and forearm. Also the lateral back of the hand and thumb, via the superficial branch.
card.injury: Wrist drop, loss of finger extension, and numbness over the first dorsal web space.
card.clinical: A midshaft humeral fracture or a long period of arm pressure (Saturday night palsy) damages it. It causes wrist drop.
card.quiz: Winds around the humerus in the spiral groove and supplies all extensors.

parts.label: Roots of brachial plexus
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Roots of the Brachial Plexus
card.summary: The five nerve roots that start the brachial plexus. They are the ventral rami of C5, C6, C7, C8 and T1.
card.from: Ventral rami of spinal nerves C5 to T1
card.course: They leave the spine between the anterior and middle scalene muscles. They then pass above the first rib toward the armpit.
card.sensory: None directly (carried by branches such as the dorsal scapular nerve)
card.injury: C5–C6 injury causes Erb palsy. C8–T1 injury causes Klumpke palsy.
card.clinical: Roots can be torn from the spinal cord in motorcycle crashes or birth traction. This is called a root avulsion.
card.quiz: Five spinal levels, C5 to T1, that feed the whole plexus.

parts.label: Subclavian nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular branches of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Nerve to Subclavius
card.group: Branches from the trunks of the brachial plexus
card.summary: A small motor nerve to the subclavius muscle under the clavicle.
card.from: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It descends in front of the plexus and subclavian artery to reach subclavius. Sometimes it sends a branch to the phrenic nerve.
card.sensory: None (motor only)
card.injury: No notable deficit.
card.clinical: Its accessory phrenic branch is present in some people and is of minor clinical importance.
card.quiz: Tiny nerve to the muscle under the clavicle.

parts.label: Superficial branch of radial nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Radial nerve.r

card.name: Radial Nerve — Superficial Branch
card.summary: The sensory branch of the radial nerve. It supplies the skin of the thumb side of the back of the hand.
card.from: Radial nerve, in front of the lateral epicondyle
card.course: It runs under brachioradialis beside the radial artery. In the lower forearm it moves to the back of the wrist and divides into dorsal digital nerves.
card.sensory: Skin of the lateral back of the hand and the proximal dorsum of the thumb and lateral two and a half fingers.
card.injury: Numbness over the thumb side of the back of the hand without any muscle weakness.
card.clinical: A tight watch band or handcuffs can compress it (Wartenberg syndrome). It causes tingling at the base of the thumb.
card.quiz: Purely sensory branch that runs under brachioradialis to the thumb side of the back of the hand.

parts.label: Superficial branch of ulnar nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g > Ulnar nerve.r

card.name: Ulnar Nerve — Superficial Branch
card.summary: The sensory branch of the ulnar nerve in the hand. It supplies the palmar skin of the little finger and half of the ring finger.
card.from: Ulnar nerve, in Guyon canal
card.course: It leaves the nerve beside the pisiform and runs into the hypothenar palm. It gives a twig to palmaris brevis and then divides into digital nerves.
card.sensory: Palmar skin of the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.
card.injury: Numbness of the palmar little finger and medial half of the ring finger.
card.clinical: Compression in Guyon canal can numb the little finger and the medial half of the ring finger.
card.quiz: Hand branch that gives sensation to the palmar side of the little finger.

parts.label: Superior lateral brachial cutaneous nerve
parts.group: Brachial plexus.g > Branches of posterior cord of brachial plexus.g > Axillary nerve.r

card.name: Superior Lateral Brachial Cutaneous Nerve
card.summary: A skin branch of the axillary nerve. It supplies the skin over the lower deltoid.
card.from: Axillary nerve (posterior cord of the brachial plexus)
card.course: It winds around the posterior border of the deltoid and pierces the deep fascia. It runs to the skin over the lateral arm.
card.sensory: Skin over the lower deltoid and the upper lateral arm (the regimental badge area).
card.injury: Numbness over the lower deltoid (regimental badge area).
card.clinical: A patch of numb skin here is a quick test of the axillary nerve after shoulder injury.
card.quiz: Skin of the regimental badge area. It is the sensory test for the axillary nerve.

parts.label: Superior trunk of brachial plexus
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular part of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Superior Trunk of the Brachial Plexus
card.summary: The highest trunk of the brachial plexus. It is formed by the C5 and C6 ventral rami.
card.from: Union of the ventral rami of C5 and C6
card.course: It forms at Erb point in the lower neck. It gives the suprascapular nerve and the nerve to subclavius, then divides into anterior and posterior divisions.
card.sensory: None directly (a conduit for fibers to later branches)
card.injury: Erb palsy: the arm hangs at the side, turned inward, with the forearm pronated (waiter-tip position).
card.clinical: Hard traction on the neck and shoulder, for example in a fall or during a difficult birth, can injure it.
card.quiz: Upper trunk, formed by C5 and C6.

parts.label: Suprascapular nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Supraclavicular branches of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Suprascapular Nerve
card.group: Branches from the trunks of the brachial plexus
card.summary: A nerve from the superior trunk. It supplies the supraspinatus and infraspinatus muscles of the rotator cuff.
card.from: Superior trunk of the brachial plexus
card.course: It passes through the suprascapular notch under the superior transverse scapular ligament. It then curves around the spine of the scapula to infraspinatus.
card.sensory: No skin supply. It supplies the shoulder joint and the acromioclavicular joint.
card.injury: Weak start of arm abduction and weak outward rotation, with wasting above and below the scapular spine.
card.clinical: Entrapment at the suprascapular notch is common in overhead athletes. It causes deep shoulder pain and weak abduction and external rotation.
card.quiz: Passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament and supplies two rotator cuff muscles.

parts.label: Ulnar nerve
parts.group: Spinal nerves.g > Brachial plexus.g > Branches of medial cord of brachial plexus.g

card.name: Ulnar Nerve
card.group: Terminal branches of the brachial plexus
card.summary: The nerve of the inner forearm and hand. It supplies most of the small muscles of the hand and the skin of the little finger side.
card.from: Medial cord of the brachial plexus
card.course: It runs down the medial arm and behind the medial epicondyle. It passes between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, then through Guyon canal at the wrist.
motor: Forearm: flexor carpi ulnaris, flexor digitorum profundus (medial half)
Hand: hypothenar muscles, third and fourth lumbricals, interossei, adductor pollicis, palmaris brevis, flexor pollicis brevis (deep head)
card.sensory: Skin of the medial one and a half digits, both palmar and dorsal, and the medial palm and back of the hand.
card.injury: Ulnar claw of the ring and little fingers, weak finger spreading, Froment sign, and numbness of the little finger.
card.clinical: Pressure behind the medial epicondyle (the funny bone) gives tingling in the little finger. Cubital tunnel syndrome is a common compression.
card.quiz: Passes behind the medial epicondyle and supplies the little finger side of the hand.

parts.label: Anterior circumflex humeral artery
parts.group: Systemic arteries.g > Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r

card.name: Anterior circumflex humeral artery
card.summary: A small branch of the axillary artery that wraps around the front of the surgical neck of the humerus.
card.from: Axillary artery (third part)
card.course: It runs laterally under coracobrachialis and the short head of biceps, then around the surgical neck. It meets the posterior circumflex artery.
branches: Ascending branch along the bicipital groove
card.clinical: A fracture of the surgical neck can injure it. Both circumflex arteries help supply the humeral head.
card.quiz: Small third-part axillary branch that passes in front of the surgical neck and sends a branch up the bicipital groove.

parts.label: Anterior circumflex humeral vein
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Anterior circumflex humeral vein
card.summary: A small vein that accompanies the anterior circumflex humeral artery.
drains: Front of the upper arm and shoulder joint
card.into: Axillary vein
card.course: It wraps around the front of the surgical neck of the humerus and empties into the axillary vein.
card.clinical: It lies close to the humeral neck, so it can be torn in surgical neck fractures.
card.quiz: Small vein that wraps in front of the surgical neck.

parts.label: Axillary artery
parts.group: Cardiovascular system.g > Systemic arteries.g > Right subclavian artery

card.name: Axillary artery
card.summary: The continuation of the subclavian artery through the armpit. Pectoralis minor divides it into three parts.
card.from: Subclavian artery (at the lateral border of the first rib)
card.course: It runs from the first rib to the lower border of teres major, where it becomes the brachial artery. Part 1 is above, part 2 behind, and part 3 below pectoralis minor.
branches: Part 2: thoraco-acromial artery and lateral thoracic artery
Part 3: subscapular, anterior circumflex humeral, and posterior circumflex humeral arteries
card.clinical: Rich anastomoses around the scapula keep the arm alive if the artery is blocked or tied between the subscapular and thoraco-acromial branches.
card.quiz: Three parts named by their relation to pectoralis minor. Ends at the lower border of teres major.

parts.label: Axillary vein
parts.group: Cardiovascular system.g > Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein

card.name: Axillary vein
card.summary: The main vein of the armpit. It lies next to the axillary artery.
drains: Arm (through the brachial and basilic veins)
card.into: Subclavian vein (at the lateral border of the first rib)
card.course: It begins where the basilic vein joins the brachial veins, at the lower border of teres major. It ends at the lateral border of the first rib.
card.clinical: A clot here, often after hard repeated arm effort, causes a swollen painful arm (effort thrombosis or Paget-Schroetter syndrome).
card.quiz: Formed by the basilic and brachial veins. Ends at the first rib as the subclavian vein.

parts.label: Basilic vein
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Basilic vein
card.group: Superficial veins of the upper limb
card.summary: The main superficial vein on the little-finger side of the arm.
drains: Medial side of the dorsal venous network
card.into: Axillary vein (by joining the brachial veins)
card.course: It runs up the medial forearm, passes in front of the medial epicondyle, and pierces the deep fascia in the mid-arm. It joins the brachial veins to form the axillary vein.
card.clinical: It is often used for PICC lines. The median cubital vein usually joins it at the elbow.
card.quiz: Little-finger-side superficial vein. Joins the brachial veins to make the axillary vein.

parts.label: Brachial artery
parts.group: Systemic arteries.g > Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r

card.name: Brachial artery
card.summary: The main artery of the arm. It is the continuation of the axillary artery.
card.from: Axillary artery (at the lower border of teres major)
card.course: It runs down the medial arm on brachialis. The median nerve crosses it from lateral to medial. In the cubital fossa it divides into the radial and ulnar arteries.
card.clinical: Its pulse and blood pressure are taken in the cubital fossa, just medial to the biceps tendon. Supracondylar fractures can damage it.
card.quiz: Continues from the axillary artery. Splits into radial and ulnar arteries at the cubital fossa.

parts.label: Brachial veins
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Brachial veins
card.summary: A pair of deep veins that run on either side of the brachial artery.
card.into: Axillary vein (after joining the basilic vein)
card.course: They begin in the cubital fossa where the radial and ulnar veins unite. They ascend with the brachial artery and join the basilic vein to form the axillary vein.
card.clinical: These deep veins are a site of deep vein thrombosis in the arm. Catheters placed in the arm often pass through them.
card.quiz: Paired veins beside the brachial artery. Form the axillary vein with the basilic vein.

parts.label: Cephalic vein
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Cephalic vein
card.group: Superficial veins of the upper limb
card.summary: The main superficial vein on the thumb side of the arm.
drains: Lateral side of the dorsal venous network
card.into: Axillary vein
card.course: It starts on the thumb side of the hand and ascends along the lateral forearm and the lateral edge of biceps. It runs in the deltopectoral groove and pierces the clavipectoral fascia to enter the axillary vein.
card.clinical: It is a common IV site, and surgeons find it in the deltopectoral groove. It is also used for dialysis fistulas.
card.quiz: Thumb-side superficial vein. Runs in the deltopectoral groove and ends in the axillary vein.

parts.label: Circumflex scapular artery
parts.group: Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r > Subscapular artery.r

card.name: Circumflex scapular artery
card.summary: A branch of the subscapular artery that winds around the lateral border of the scapula.
card.from: Subscapular artery
card.course: It passes backward through the triangular space, between subscapularis, teres minor, and teres major. Then it enters the infraspinous fossa.
card.clinical: It joins the suprascapular artery in the scapular anastomosis, a key collateral route around the shoulder.
card.quiz: Passes through the triangular space to reach the back of the scapula.

parts.label: Circumflex scapular vein
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Circumflex scapular vein
card.summary: A vein that accompanies the circumflex scapular artery around the border of the scapula.
drains: Muscles on the back of the scapula
card.into: Subscapular vein
card.course: It follows the artery through the triangular space and joins the subscapular vein, which drains into the axillary vein.
card.clinical: It travels in the triangular space with its artery. It matters mainly in surgery around the scapula.
card.quiz: Travels with an artery through the triangular space.

parts.label: Common interosseous artery
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Ulnar artery.r

card.name: Common interosseous artery
card.summary: A short branch of the ulnar artery that divides into the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.
card.from: Ulnar artery (in the upper forearm)
card.course: It is only about 1 cm long. It ends near the upper border of the interosseous membrane by splitting into two branches.
supplies: Deep flexor and extensor muscles of the forearm
card.clinical: It is the source of blood to the deep forearm. Damage in the proximal forearm can contribute to compartment syndrome.
card.quiz: Very short trunk. Splits into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

parts.label: Common palmar digital arteries
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Ulnar artery.r

card.name: Common palmar digital arteries
card.summary: Three arteries that leave the superficial palmar arch. They run toward the webs between the fingers.
card.from: Superficial palmar arch (with contributions from the palmar metacarpal arteries)
card.course: They run distally over the lumbricals toward the webs of the second to fourth spaces. Each splits into two proper palmar digital arteries.
supplies: Adjacent sides of the index, middle, ring, and little fingers
card.clinical: They lie close to the common digital nerves. A deep palm cut can injure both.
card.quiz: Three arteries from the superficial arch. Each splits at a finger web.

parts.label: Deep brachial artery
parts.group: Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r

card.name: Deep brachial artery
card.summary: The largest branch of the brachial artery. It supplies the back of the arm.
card.from: Brachial artery (near the lower border of teres major)
card.course: It passes behind the humerus in the radial groove with the radial nerve, between the heads of triceps. It ends as the middle and radial collateral arteries.
card.clinical: A mid-shaft humerus fracture in the radial groove can injure this artery and the radial nerve together.
card.quiz: Travels with the radial nerve in the radial groove.

parts.label: Deep palmar arch
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Radial artery.r

card.name: Deep palmar arch
card.summary: An arterial arch deep in the palm. The radial artery forms most of it.
card.from: Radial artery (completed by the deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery)
card.course: It crosses the palm at the bases of the metacarpals, deep to the long flexor tendons. It lies about 1 cm closer to the wrist than the superficial arch.
card.clinical: It lies deeper than the superficial arch. Its main source is the radial artery, so radial injuries can reduce its flow.
card.quiz: Mainly from the radial artery. Deep to the flexor tendons at the metacarpal bases.

parts.label: Deep venous palmar arch
parts.group: Axillary vein.r > Brachial veins.r > Radial veins.r

card.name: Deep venous palmar arch
card.summary: A pair of veins that accompany the deep palmar arterial arch.
card.into: Radial and ulnar veins (deep veins that run with the arteries)
card.course: It lies deep in the palm at the bases of the metacarpals, beside the deep palmar arterial arch.
card.clinical: It is a deep vein, so it cannot be seen through the skin.
card.quiz: Deep veins that accompany the radial-side arterial arch of the palm.

parts.label: Dorsal carpal anastomosis
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Radial artery.r

card.name: Dorsal carpal arch (anastomosis)
card.summary: A network of arteries on the back of the wrist. It is formed by the radial and ulnar dorsal carpal branches.
card.from: Dorsal carpal branches of the radial and ulnar arteries (with the anterior and posterior interosseous arteries)
card.course: It lies on the back of the carpus under the extensor tendons. It gives off the second to fourth dorsal metacarpal arteries.
supplies: Back of the hand (through its branches)
card.clinical: It provides collateral flow around the wrist and feeds the arteries of the back of the hand.
card.quiz: Network on the back of the wrist. Source of the dorsal metacarpal arteries.

parts.mesh: Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery.r
parts.label: Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Ulnar artery.r

card.name: Dorsal carpal branch of the ulnar artery
card.summary: A branch of the ulnar artery that winds to the back of the wrist.
card.from: Ulnar artery (just above the pisiform)
card.course: It passes deep to the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon, around the ulnar side of the wrist, and joins the dorsal carpal network.
card.clinical: It helps form the dorsal carpal network. This is a collateral route if the radial or ulnar artery is injured.
card.quiz: Winds around the little-finger side of the wrist to the network on the back of the carpus.

parts.label: Dorsal digital arteries of hand
parts.group: Radial artery.r > Dorsal carpal anastomosis.r > Dorsal metacarpal arteries.r

card.name: Dorsal digital arteries of the hand
card.summary: Small arteries on the backs of the fingers. They arise from the dorsal metacarpal arteries.
card.from: Dorsal metacarpal arteries (also directly from the radial artery for the thumb)
card.course: Each pair runs along the sides of a finger on its back. They usually reach only the proximal and middle segments.
supplies: Skin of the back of the fingers (proximal parts)
Extensor tendons and joints of the fingers
card.clinical: The fingertips are mainly supplied from the palmar side, so loss of the dorsal arteries rarely harms the fingertip.
card.quiz: Paired arteries on the backs of the fingers. Come from the dorsal metacarpal arteries.

parts.label: Dorsal digital veins of hand
parts.group: Axillary vein.r > Cephalic vein.r > Dorsal venous network of hand.r

card.name: Dorsal digital veins of the hand
card.summary: Small veins on the backs of the fingers. They collect blood from the fingers.
card.into: Dorsal venous network of the hand (through the dorsal metacarpal veins)
card.course: They run along the sides of the fingers and join near the webs to form dorsal metacarpal veins. These empty into the dorsal venous network.
card.clinical: They join the network used for hand IV access. Swelling of the hand shows first on the back, where these veins lie.
card.quiz: Superficial veins on the backs of the fingers. They feed the dorsal venous network.

parts.label: Dorsal metacarpal arteries
parts.group: Brachial artery.r > Radial artery.r > Dorsal carpal anastomosis.r

card.name: Dorsal metacarpal arteries
card.summary: Three or four small arteries on the back of the hand. They run over the dorsal interossei.
card.from: Dorsal carpal arch (the first comes from the radial artery)
card.course: They run distally on the dorsal interossei. Each divides into two dorsal digital arteries near the finger webs. Perforating branches join the deep palmar arch.
branches: Perforating branches to the deep palmar arch
card.clinical: Perforating branches link the back and palm of the hand, so injury to one side may be partly offset by the other.
card.quiz: Run on the dorsal interossei. Each splits into two dorsal digital arteries.

parts.label: Dorsal venous network of hand
parts.group: Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r > Cephalic vein.r

card.name: Dorsal venous network of the hand
card.summary: A web of veins under the skin on the back of the hand. It gives rise to the cephalic and basilic veins.
card.into: Cephalic vein (lateral side) and basilic vein (medial side)
card.course: It lies on the back of the hand. Its lateral part continues up the arm as the cephalic vein and its medial part as the basilic vein.
card.clinical: The veins are easy to see here, so the back of the hand is a common site for IV cannulation.
card.quiz: Web of veins on the back of the hand. Gives rise to the cephalic and basilic veins.

parts.label: Inferior ulnar collateral artery
parts.group: Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r

card.name: Inferior ulnar collateral artery
card.summary: A branch of the brachial artery just above the elbow. It passes in front of the medial epicondyle.
card.from: Brachial artery (about 5 cm above the elbow)
card.course: It runs medially in front of the medial epicondyle and meets the anterior ulnar recurrent artery. It also joins the superior ulnar collateral artery.
card.clinical: It is a link in the elbow anastomosis. This network helps the forearm if the brachial artery is blocked below the collaterals.
card.quiz: Passes in front of the medial epicondyle. Meets the anterior ulnar recurrent artery.

parts.label: Lateral thoracic artery
parts.group: Systemic arteries.g > Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r

card.name: Lateral thoracic artery
card.summary: A branch of the axillary artery that runs down the side of the chest wall.
card.from: Axillary artery (second part); sometimes the subscapular artery
card.course: It follows the lateral border of pectoralis minor down to the side of the chest, in company with the long thoracic nerve.
card.clinical: It supplies the outer breast. Surgeons see it during axillary node dissection, and it must be protected near the long thoracic nerve.
card.quiz: Descends along the lateral edge of pectoralis minor to serratus anterior.

parts.label: Lateral thoracic vein
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Lateral thoracic vein
card.summary: A vein that drains the side of the chest wall and the outer breast.
card.into: Axillary vein
card.course: It follows the lateral thoracic artery along the lateral border of pectoralis minor.
card.clinical: It links with the superficial thoraco-epigastric vein. This gives a route between the upper and lower body if a main vein is blocked.
card.quiz: Drains the side of the chest. Follows the lower edge of pectoralis minor.

parts.label: Median antebrachial vein
parts.group: Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r > Basilic vein.r

card.name: Median antebrachial vein
card.group: Superficial veins of the upper limb
card.summary: A small superficial vein that runs up the middle of the front of the forearm.
drains: Palmar venous plexus of the hand
card.into: Median cubital vein, basilic vein, or cephalic vein (this varies)
card.course: It starts from the palmar venous plexus and ascends the front of the forearm between the cephalic and basilic veins. Its end varies from person to person.
card.clinical: It is sometimes used for IV access when other veins are not available. Its pattern varies a lot.
card.quiz: Runs up the middle of the front of the forearm. Its ending varies.

parts.label: Median cubital vein
parts.group: Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r > Basilic vein.r

card.name: Median cubital vein
card.group: Superficial veins of the upper limb
card.summary: A short superficial vein that links the cephalic and basilic veins across the front of the elbow.
card.into: Basilic vein
card.course: It runs obliquely from the cephalic vein up and medially over the cubital fossa. It lies on top of the bicipital aponeurosis.
card.clinical: It is the most common site for blood draws and IV access. The bicipital aponeurosis protects the brachial artery below it.
card.quiz: Common site for blood draws. Connects the cephalic and basilic veins at the elbow.

parts.label: Middle collateral artery
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Deep brachial artery.r

card.name: Middle collateral artery
card.summary: A terminal branch of the deep brachial artery. It runs down the back of the arm toward the elbow.
card.from: Deep brachial artery
card.course: It descends in the medial head of triceps behind the elbow and meets the recurrent interosseous artery.
card.clinical: It joins the arterial network around the elbow. This network keeps the forearm supplied if the brachial artery is blocked.
card.quiz: Goes down the triceps to meet the recurrent interosseous artery.

parts.mesh: Palmar carpal branch of radial artery.r
parts.label: Palmar carpal branch of radial artery
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Radial artery.r

card.name: Palmar carpal branch of the radial artery
card.summary: A small branch of the radial artery that crosses the front of the wrist.
card.from: Radial artery (near the lower border of pronator quadratus)
card.course: It runs medially across the front of the carpus, deep to the flexor tendons. It joins the palmar carpal branch of the ulnar artery.
card.clinical: Together with the ulnar branch it forms the palmar carpal arch, a collateral network at the wrist.
card.quiz: Small branch of the thumb-side forearm artery that crosses the front of the carpus.

parts.label: Palmar digital veins
parts.group: Brachial veins.r > Ulnar veins.r > Superficial venous palmar arch.r

card.name: Palmar digital veins
card.summary: Small veins on the palm side of the fingers. They accompany the proper palmar digital arteries.
card.into: Superficial venous palmar arch (through the common palmar digital veins)
card.course: They run along the fingers and join near the finger webs to form common palmar digital veins. Many also drain to the back of the hand.
card.clinical: Much finger blood drains to the back of the hand, so a tight band at the finger base can cause swelling.
card.quiz: Small veins on the palm side of the fingers. Many also drain to the back of the hand.

parts.label: Palmar metacarpal arteries
parts.group: Brachial artery.r > Radial artery.r > Deep palmar arch.r

card.name: Palmar metacarpal arteries
card.summary: Three small arteries that leave the deep palmar arch. They run toward the fingers on the palmar interossei.
card.from: Deep palmar arch
card.course: They pass distally along the second to fourth metacarpal spaces. Near the finger webs they join the common palmar digital arteries.
card.clinical: They link the deep and superficial arches, which helps the hand keep its blood flow.
card.quiz: Three arteries from the deep arch. They join the common palmar digital arteries.

parts.label: Pectoral branches of thoraco-acromial artery
parts.group: Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r > Thoraco-acromial artery.r

card.name: Pectoral branches of the thoraco-acromial artery
card.summary: These branches of the thoraco-acromial artery supply the pectoral muscles. They also help feed the breast.
card.from: Thoraco-acromial artery
card.course: They run down between pectoralis major and pectoralis minor and enter the deep surface of both muscles.
card.clinical: They are cut or cauterized in surgery on the pectoral muscles. They are also part of the blood supply that surgeons use for pectoral flaps.
card.quiz: Run between the two chest muscles; they come from the short trunk off the second part of the axillary artery.

parts.label: Posterior circumflex humeral artery
parts.group: Systemic arteries.g > Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r

card.name: Posterior circumflex humeral artery
card.summary: A branch of the axillary artery that passes through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve.
card.from: Axillary artery (third part)
card.course: It leaves the axilla through the quadrangular space and winds around the surgical neck of the humerus under deltoid.
card.clinical: A surgical neck fracture or shoulder dislocation can injure it together with the axillary nerve.
card.quiz: Travels with the axillary nerve through the quadrangular space.

parts.label: Posterior circumflex humeral vein
parts.group: Systemic veins.g > Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r

card.name: Posterior circumflex humeral vein
card.summary: A small vein that accompanies the posterior circumflex humeral artery.
card.into: Axillary vein
card.course: It passes through the quadrangular space with the axillary nerve and artery, then joins the axillary vein.
card.clinical: It can be damaged with the axillary nerve in a shoulder dislocation or surgical neck fracture.
card.quiz: Travels with the axillary nerve through the quadrangular space.

parts.label: Posterior interosseus artery
parts.group: Brachial artery.r > Ulnar artery.r > Common interosseous artery.r

card.name: Posterior interosseous artery
card.summary: The artery of the extensor compartment of the forearm. It passes through the gap above the interosseous membrane.
card.from: Common interosseous artery
card.course: It passes backward above the interosseous membrane and runs between the superficial and deep extensor muscles. It gives off the recurrent interosseous artery.
supplies: Dorsal wrist (through the dorsal carpal network)
card.clinical: It travels with the deep branch of the radial nerve, so injuries to the proximal forearm can affect both.
card.quiz: Goes backward above the interosseous membrane to the extensor muscles.

parts.label: Proper palmar digital arteries
parts.group: Brachial artery.r > Ulnar artery.r > Common palmar digital arteries.r

card.name: Proper palmar digital arteries
card.summary: The arteries that run along the sides of each finger on the palm side. They give the fingers most of their blood.
card.from: Common palmar digital arteries (for the thumb and index finger, branches of the radial artery)
card.course: A pair runs along each finger beside the flexor sheath, just behind the proper palmar digital nerves. They join over the fingertip.
card.clinical: Digital nerve blocks are given at the base of the finger, close to these vessels. Deep finger cuts can sever both artery and nerve.
card.quiz: Run on both sides of each finger on the palm side, behind the digital nerves.

parts.label: Radial artery
parts.group: Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r

card.name: Radial artery
card.summary: The smaller terminal branch of the brachial artery. It runs along the thumb side of the forearm.
card.from: Brachial artery (in the cubital fossa)
card.course: It descends under brachioradialis, then lies beside the flexor carpi radialis tendon at the wrist. It crosses the anatomical snuffbox and enters the palm to form the deep palmar arch.
branches: Princeps pollicis and radialis indicis arteries
card.clinical: The radial pulse is felt lateral to the flexor carpi radialis tendon. The Allen test checks flow through the radial and ulnar arteries.
card.quiz: Pulse taken at the wrist. Passes through the anatomical snuffbox.

parts.label: Radial collateral artery
parts.group: Axillary artery.r > Brachial artery.r > Deep brachial artery.r

card.name: Radial collateral artery
card.summary: A terminal branch of the deep brachial artery. It follows the radial nerve to the front of the lateral epicondyle.
card.from: Deep brachial artery
card.course: It accompanies the radial nerve through the lateral intermuscular septum. It then runs in front of the lateral epicondyle and meets the radial recurrent artery.
card.clinical: It is part of the elbow anastomosis that provides collateral flow around the joint.
card.quiz: Accompanies the radial nerve to the lateral elbow. Meets the radial recurrent artery.

parts.label: Radial veins
parts.group: Right subclavian vein > Axillary vein.r > Brachial veins.r

card.name: Radial veins
card.summary: A pair of deep veins that accompany the radial artery.
drains: Deep structures of the lateral forearm
card.into: Brachial veins (after joining the ulnar veins)
card.course: They start from the deep venous palmar arch and run up the lateral forearm beside the radial artery. They unite with the ulnar veins near the elbow.
card.clinical: Because they are small and deep, they are rarely used for needle access. They matter when a radial artery line is placed.
card.quiz: Paired deep veins on the thumb side of the forearm that start from the deep venous palmar arch.

parts.label: Recurrent interosseus artery
parts.group: Brachial artery.r > Ulnar artery.r > Common interosseous artery.r

card.name: Recurrent interosseous artery
card.summary: A branch of the posterior interosseous artery that runs back up to the back of the elbow.
card.from: Posterior interosseous artery
card.course: It ascends behind the elbow, deep to anconeus, and meets the middle collateral artery.
card.clinical: It joins the middle collateral artery in the elbow anastomosis, giving the forearm a backup blood supply.
card.quiz: Runs up behind the elbow to meet the middle collateral artery.

parts.label: subclavian artery
parts.group: Cardiovascular system.g > Systemic arteries.g

card.name: Subclavian artery (right)
card.group: Great arteries of the upper limb
card.summary: The main artery to the right upper limb. It also sends branches to the neck, brain, and chest wall.
card.from: Brachiocephalic trunk (on the left side, directly from the aortic arch)
card.course: On the right it starts behind the sternoclavicular joint. It arches over the first rib, behind scalenus anterior, and becomes the axillary artery at the lateral border of the rib.
supplies: Brain and neck (via vertebral and thyrocervical branches)
card.clinical: Subclavian steal: a blockage before the vertebral origin can reverse vertebral flow. The person may feel dizzy when using the arm.
card.quiz: Arises from the brachiocephalic trunk on the right. Becomes the axillary artery at the first rib.

parts.label: subclavian vein
parts.group: Cardiovascular system.g > Systemic veins.g

card.name: Subclavian vein (right)
card.group: Great veins of the upper limb
card.summary: The large vein that carries blood from the arm toward the heart. It continues from the axillary vein.
drains: Whole upper limb (through the axillary vein)
card.into: Brachiocephalic vein (by joining the internal jugular vein)
card.course: It begins at the lateral border of the first rib and arches over the rib in front of scalenus anterior. The artery passes behind that muscle.
card.clinical: It is a common site for central venous catheters. A needle that goes too deep may puncture the lung.
card.quiz: Passes in front of scalenus anterior. Joins the internal jugular to form the brachiocephalic vein.

parts.label: Subscapular artery
parts.group: Systemic arteries.g > Right subclavian artery > Axillary artery.r

card.name: Subscapular artery
card.summary: The largest branch of the axillary artery. It runs along the lower edge of the subscapularis muscle.
card.from: Axillary artery (third part)
card.course: It descends along the lateral border of subscapularis. About 2 to 3 cm from its origin it gives off the circumflex scapular artery and continues as the thoracodorsal artery.
card.clinical: It links the axillary artery to the scapular anastomosis. This route can carry blood around a blockage higher in the axillary artery.
